# Workspace access

[Encrypted browser recovery](sealed-save-journal.md) additionally verifies the complete owner before sealing or opening request contents. It derives tenant/subject from the actual API access response, requires staff workspace access, and binds organization and the API-validated signed Clerk session. A caller cannot select another operator’s scope or relabel a captured envelope to open it. Encryption does not grant permission to apply or stop the original business operation.

[Browser save restoration](browser-save-journal.md) opens only after API-verified tenant/subject access and scopes retained input to that operator, authentication mode, organization and Clerk session where applicable. Shared saves additionally bind the reviewed tenant/subject at the gateway using the same captured upstream identity as the forwarded POST. A changed credential cookie cannot redirect a retained body into another tenant. This display/replay guard supplements ordinary API authorization; local browser data is not an authorization boundary.

[Resolving an uncertain original save](save-resolution.md) requires `saves.recover` plus the original route’s capability. Operations, finance, integration and administrator roles receive `saves.recover`; viewer and partner roles do not. Resolution cannot grant authority to apply a business operation. The verified tenant/actor and canonical original path/body/key determine the receipt or stop; clients cannot override identity or choose an internal operation.

[Control tower](control-tower.md) reads use `workspace.read`. Named self-claim, notes, follow-up changes, bounded deferral, release, and explicit reconciliation require `operations.write`. Only administrators have `operations.configure` for tracking policy or may release another owner. Case requests bind the authenticated subject, reviewed source/active state, and case version before mutation; a client cannot assign another person or mark an active source condition resolved. Partner roles cannot read cases, private notes, owners, policy, or metrics.

[Native movement time corrections](movement-corrections.md) require `operations.write`. Carrier, customer, viewer, finance-only, and integration roles cannot correct a carrier report. Staff readers can inspect the original source and correction evidence; scoped partner timelines expose only original/effective times and a correction marker. Named review, exact source/predecessor, current load version, chronology, and financial locks are enforced server-side.

[Intermediate stop service](multi-stop.md) requires `operations.write` for staff recording/corrections or `portal.carrier.report` for the current assigned carrier's own publication. Customer, viewer, finance-only, and integration roles cannot assert service. The server derives tender, actor, recording time, and evidence digest; staff corrections retain the entire original chain.

The API authorizes every protected endpoint using its registered route, before reading request bodies, replaying idempotency receipts, or contacting business upstream services. Staff identity verification consults Clerk before granting that business access. New routes remain denied until explicitly assigned a capability. Browser controls reflect the same capability list returned by the API; changing the operations perspective never changes access.

Staff can use the existing StateSet Clerk instance through [the implemented SSO workflow](sso.md). The API validates signed sessions, reads live membership/status, and maps explicitly approved organizations/roles to existing tenants. Browser claims and public organization metadata cannot grant a tenant or role. Static credentials below remain supported for explicit service access and credential-mode deployments.

[Carrier rate confirmations](carrier-rate-confirmations.md) require `operations.write` for issuance, actual external handoff attestation, erroneous-evidence retraction, and coordination resolution. All tenant staff readers may inspect/download the retained document and evidence. Prices, carrier, issuer, HTML/hash, and actor derive server-side. An external handoff cannot be recorded by finance/integration/viewer roles; recording it is separate from carrier acceptance or any automatic delivery.

[Cancellation fees](cancellations.md) use `charges.write` for proposals and `finance.write` for approval/rejection/reversal. All staff readers can inspect their retained agreement/decision history. Integration credentials cannot assert human carrier release or fee confirmation. Existing finance permissions govern separate invoice, bank, refund, and credit-application targets.

[Quoting and carrier procurement](quotes.md) require `operations.write` for drafts/revisions, actual offer/decision evidence, booking, reconfirmation, and replacement procurement. All staff readers can inspect/download quotes. Viewer, finance-only, and integration roles cannot assert a customer agreement or purchase rate. Quote/load versions and existing-source plan/ownership checks apply before mutation; organization-bound requests/downloads use the same gateway identity controls.

[Carrier lane agreements](carrier-contracts.md) use `operations.write` for recording/revising/withdrawing reviewed external terms and confirming capacity at a sourced rate. Every tenant staff reader can evaluate and inspect/download the private catalogue. Carrier/customer portal roles cannot use these staff routes or receive private contract terms/evidence. The server derives the exact rate/carrier/source revision, verifies the original hashes and reviewed versions, and retains the authenticated capacity confirmer separately from the agreement's original source actor. Imported replacement procurement uses the existing fresh canonical Sync check and transaction-fenced source grant.

[Commerce source review](source.md) requires `operations.write` for refresh and recorded customer transport decisions. All staff readers can inspect original/latest order evidence and review history. Finance-only and integration-only roles cannot authorize transport against a source change.

[Customer amendments](customer-amendments.md) also require `operations.write` for proposals, customer/source consent, and activation. All staff readers can inspect the original/successor agreements; historic superseded agreements cannot be revived by reconfirmation or replacement procurement.

Configure separate random credentials for people and services:

```dotenv
FREIGHT_API_KEYS_JSON='{"replace-with-a-unique-random-operations-token":{"tenant_id":"your-tenant","subject":"user:dispatcher-1","role":"operations"},"replace-with-a-unique-random-finance-token":{"tenant_id":"your-tenant","subject":"user:accountant-1","role":"finance"}}'
```

Tokens must have 32–512 printable ASCII characters without whitespace. Tenant IDs contain 1–100 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, or periods. Scoped entries require a nonempty subject (at most 100 characters) and an explicit recognized role. Unknown fields, misspelled roles, and missing roles fail startup. Configuration errors do not print credential values.

| Role          | Read tenant workspace | Plan, dispatch, master data, sync import | Enter, correct, approve invoices; prepare settlement | Receive normalized EDI events | Retry inbound/outbound work |
| ------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `viewer`      | Yes                   | —                                        | —                                                    | —                             | —                           |
| `operations`  | Yes                   | Yes                                      | —                                                    | —                             | Yes                         |
| `finance`     | Yes                   | —                                        | Yes                                                  | —                             | —                           |
| `integration` | Yes                   | —                                        | —                                                    | Yes                           | Yes                         |
| `admin`       | Yes                   | Yes                                      | Yes                                                  | Yes                           | Yes                         |

All these roles are for tenant staff or trusted tenant services and can read the complete tenant workspace, including financial and carrier evidence. Use separate `carrier`/`customer` identities with required server-owned `counterparty_id` for the [partner portal](partner-portal.md). Those roles cannot read the tenant workspace or staff routes. Carrier access is limited to explicitly published offers/documents for that carrier and native responses to current offers, current-assignment physical tracking/POD submission under `portal.carrier.report`, and exact downloads of its own submitted files; customer access includes its shipments, issued invoices, and explicitly published quote revisions/documents. Only the customer role has `portal.customer.quote.respond` for native decisions and scoped canonical source verification. Customer acceptance cannot book/activate transport or mutate procurement; those remain operations actions. Staff roles cannot select a counterparty to enter the portal. Reading upstream order candidates requires operations permission. Integration retry can apply authenticated carrier invoice evidence, but cannot approve invoices or prepare settlements. Signed EDI webhooks use their independent versioned HMAC credentials and are not bearer endpoints.

Tender withdrawal, carrier release requests/confirmation/retention, and carrier conflict resolution require `operations.write` (`operations` or `admin`). These actions record the authenticated subject and require the current load version. Integration credentials may submit signed carrier evidence but cannot confirm a human carrier release or resolve custody conflicts. Finance approval is blocked by unresolved tender incidents.

Operations also publishes exact [carrier release requests](tenders.md#authenticated-carrier-release) and applies retained native acknowledgements under `operations.write`. Only scoped carrier identities have `portal.carrier.release` to answer their own current published request; this grants no staff release or custody-resolution powers. Native evidence keeps the original carrier subject/time/contact/hash even when operations applies it later, with a separately recorded application actor/time. Pickup, financial, deadline, and live handoff checks still govern application. Carrier downloads use `portal.read` and expose only that carrier's published release documents. Finance-only, integration, viewer, and customer roles cannot publish, apply, or impersonate a native carrier response.

Appointment booking/rescheduling/cancellation and gate evidence/corrections also require `operations.write`, load-version checks, and server-recorded subjects. Readers can inspect the original appointment and gate history. An integration credential cannot assert a human facility confirmation or edit gate evidence through these routes. Gate times do not create finance approval or charges.

`operations`, `finance`, and `admin` additionally receive `documents.write` to upload immutable shipment files. Every tenant role can download its tenant's files. Document and external POD reviews require `finance.write`; changing a POD attachment requires `operations.write`. Uploading or reviewing a file does not grant the other role's capabilities. Invoice approval and settlement require accepted delivery evidence and verify stored byte integrity before committing.

Customer invoice creation/revision/issuance/voiding, supplemental customer billing and explicit corrections, credits (including paid-customer credits with actual confirmation), billing issuer configuration, and bank reconciliation/reversal including customer refunds require `finance.write`. Tenant roles can read invoice statements and the freight journal export. The API fixes identity before idempotency lookup and applies the same tenant boundary to these records. No role here initiates bank transfers.

`operations`, `finance`, and `admin` receive `charges.write` to propose documented additions or explicit corrections. Approving/rejecting/voiding charge decisions requires `finance.write`. Operations cannot approve its proposal through a different perspective, forged actor field, or replay. Every mutation checks current load/charge versions and records the server-authenticated subject. A named finance decision verifies the counterparty agreement; it does not automatically send that agreement, approve POD, or execute a payment.

Carrier financial adjustment creation/approval/rejection/reversal, canonical invoice classification/dismissal, and carrier-refund bank reconciliation require `finance.write`. Signed EDI/integration credentials can retain an additional document but cannot classify it or post a payable. Every tenant role can inspect its tenant's retained financial evidence. Counterparty confirmation and posting/reversal actors are recorded separately; the original decision is preserved.

Carrier credit applications, reversals, and explicit corrections also require `finance.write`. Operations/integration credentials cannot reallocate financial credits. Every tenant role may inspect the confirmation and source/target history; the browser hides writes through disabled controls and the API independently denies them. The caller cannot supply the carrier, currency, status, or recorded subject. Source/target settlement versions protect against competing allocations, payouts, and refunds.

Audit events store the verified subject. In credential mode, rotate a person's credential without changing its configured subject to preserve attribution; the browser stores that credential in an encrypted cookie. Configuration changes require restarting every API replica, and old cookies cannot bypass them. In Clerk mode, the immutable Clerk user ID supplies the subject; membership/role/session changes apply to subsequent requests through live verification. The SDK uses its short-lived session cookie/token design and Clerk sign-out rather than the eight-hour credential cookie. Do not share identities if individual accountability matters.

Legacy entries such as `"token":"tenant-id"` retain administrator access and use a one-way credential fingerprint as their audit subject. Migrate these to explicit subject/role objects before issuing limited access. Demo access is also an administrator of synthetic demo data.

Static grants and Clerk-backed dynamic staff memberships are enforced. Clerk instance/domain/role enrollment and live SSO commissioning remain deployment work. Counterparty filtering is enforced in the partner portal. Partner enrollment/invitations, finer partner/facility scopes, and enforced separation between invoice entry and approval remain additional identity/policy work. Finance approval still requires the existing business checks for matched amounts, delivery, and POD evidence.

[Partner file sharing](documents.md#share-original-files-with-partners) uses `documents.write` for operations/finance/admin publication and revocation. Carrier invoice/rate files additionally require finance/admin for creation and cannot target customers. The server owns the recipient/tender/actor/role and checks original bytes transactionally. Partner downloads under `portal.read` are limited to that role/counterparty's exact grants; they check revocation and bytes and commit an authorization audit under the same tenant lock. Staff readers retain their existing generic file access. Content review and revocation reasons remain private; downloaded copies and independent published documents are unaffected by revoking a grant.

## Dialog background isolation

The shared staff and partner dialog keeps the active task available while making background sibling subtrees inert and hidden from accessibility queries. It follows the dialog’s ancestor path, so dialogs embedded in shipment details and dialogs rendered through a portal use the same boundary. A nested dialog owns interaction until it closes; its parent temporarily reports `aria-modal="false"`, then regains its original modal state. Existing Tab, Shift+Tab, Escape, focus restoration and page-scroll behavior remain covered by the browser suite.

The boundary observes newly mounted background controls and restores the exact prior `inert`, `aria-hidden` and parent `aria-modal` attributes on close or unmount. Previously hidden controls stay hidden; an original `aria-hidden="false"` value is preserved. Native inert prevents background programmatic focus as well as ordinary interaction. Server-side tenant and role checks continue to decide who may submit each operation.

Two actual preceding-production Chromium cases reproduce background focus and accessibility exposure at 1280- and 390-pixel widths. Both pass on the new build. A third case opens a real nested carrier-confirmation form, verifies parent isolation and focus restoration, mounts a late background control, restores preexisting attributes and confirms that cancellation neither issues a carrier document nor changes the load version. All 108 production-browser cases pass against the new image’s exact compiled application and traced dependencies, under the restricted PostgreSQL verification-only login.

The first full attempt remains failed: 95 cases passed, six failed and seven did not run. Five cases used accessibility-filtered queries to inspect background data during a dialog; six selectors now explicitly include hidden background nodes while retaining every content, version, original-request, overload and replay assertion. The other failure was an isolated fixture’s missing historical qualification receipts; exact original receipts were copied and their existing hash checks retained. The full subsequent suite has zero skips, failures or retries. The earlier missing relative-identity fixture and incorrect exact navigation-title selector are also retained as failed attempts.

Existing preview processes on ports 36445/36446 continue to use their preceding compiled artifact. The qualified new web image and application tree are recorded in the integration receipt for a separate deployment. These synthetic Chromium checks improve a specific interaction boundary; independent keyboard/screen-reader trials, measured operator task completion and onboarding/support outcomes still require operating evidence.

## Clerk SDK migration

Six new production-browser cases cover SDK loading, staff and mobile partner access, canonical role mapping, organization changes with delayed old data, rejected token requests with an open draft, pending sessions, and encrypted recovery cleanup after session replacement. The tests use the actual bundled React provider and hooks plus the real signed-token gateway/API. Only the remote ClerkJS and hosted UI boundary is controlled; these checks do not certify a real Clerk application, account, hosted interface or public callback. Two additional Node cases verify that token errors propagate without forwarding a command or fabricating a sign-out response.

The initial before-upgrade browser run failed because the owned remote client omitted the organization prefetch method required by both SDK versions. Its traces remain retained; adding that explicit method made all six cases pass on SDK 5 before running the upgraded SDK. The full updated suite then passes without retries or skipped cases. The qualified image uses Node 22.23.3; host browser tests use Node 22.18.0 with the image’s exact compiled JavaScript and traced production dependencies. The fresh locked image install reports zero npm audit findings; operating-system review and live commissioning remain separate evidence gates.

# Freight API

The workspace root includes an `operations` summary with source-derived counts, response sample denominators, evidence status, and tracking policy. It omits issue histories. [Control tower API](control-tower.md#access-and-api) documents paginated filtered lists and separate complete history reads. Case actions bind the exact reviewed version, source digest, active/cleared state, and authenticated subject; source changes return 409. Ownership never modifies physical shipment or financial state.

Each staff load includes `execution_timeline: {consistent, evidence_valid, record_count, conflicts, stops}`. Facts expose kinds, effective actual UTC times, source, references, and actors; corrected native facts additionally retain `original_observed_at` and the private current correction. Staff `movement_sources` contains exact original reports/digests and full correction history; the workspace root includes `movement_corrections`. Current carrier offers and customer shipments receive original/effective times and a correction marker without staff proof/identity fields. Gate/service/native tracking and correction requests share one chronology validator. Conflicts or invalid correction evidence feed `route_attention` and hold delivery readiness/final Sync writeback. See [shared execution timeline](execution-timeline.md) and [movement correction request/evidence](movement-corrections.md#atomic-source-bound-correction).

All `/v1/*` routes require `Authorization: Bearer <service credential or Clerk session JWT>`. Static service credentials fix their tenant/subject/role. Staff JWTs must pass the configured Clerk signature/issuer/origin/time checks and live session/membership verification; server-owned organization and role mappings fix the canonical Freight tenant and capabilities. Mutations use an `Idempotency-Key` of 1–200 characters; the [original-save resolver](save-resolution.md) instead identifies the original request with `request_key` in its body. Replaying the same logical request returns its original result; changing the request under that key returns 409. Domain validation errors return 422, missing entities 404, and stale-version conflicts 409. Mutation responses use `{data, replayed}`; the workspace endpoint returns the workspace object directly.

[Carrier contract API](carrier-contracts.md#api) adds agreement creation/revision/withdrawal and exact original statements under `/v1/carrier-contracts`; `/v1/quotes/{id}/contract-rates` evaluates applicability, and `/contract-offers` or `/contract-reprocure` records fresh capacity at the server-derived inclusive price. Staff workspace `carrier_contracts` excludes HTML; carrier offers/awards retain optional exact `rate_source`. Partner projections exclude the private catalogue and agreement evidence.

A role without permission receives 403 before mutation, replay, or business-upstream access. Staff authentication consults Clerk before granting business access; provider failure returns a generic 503 and cannot fall back to a stale membership. Pending/invalid/revoked sessions receive 401; missing/unmapped memberships receive 403. The SSO gateway sends `X-Freight-Identity-Mode: clerk` to prohibit static credential fallback, and `X-Freight-Organization-Id` to guard the organization that rendered a request/download. A mismatched signed organization is rejected. Neither header can grant identity or a tenant. Workspace responses include `access: {role, subject, capabilities}` for the current principal. Staff audit subjects are `clerk:<user ID>`. See [SSO configuration and verification](sso.md), [access controls and the role matrix](access.md).

Supported modes: `FTL`, `LTL`. Equipment: `Dry van`, `Reefer`, `Flatbed`. Each shipment has one currency (USD by default; see [multi-currency](multi-currency.md)); money is integer minor units in that currency, never floating-point arithmetic in the API/domain.

Plans optionally accept `intermediate_stops: [{id, kind, stop}]`, with up to eighteen stable `stop_` IDs between origin and destination. These stops use the existing stop shape, kind `pickup` or `delivery`, and ordered dates. Their actual service endpoints require `{expected_load_version, stop_id, observed_at, contact, reference, note}`. See [multi-stop execution](multi-stop.md).

Stop street/postal details may be absent from legacy records and API drafts; new tenders require both. Stop country defaults to `US` when missing. Wire limits are facility 60, city 30, each of up to two street lines 55, postal code 15, and uppercase two-letter state/country. Wire fields are ASCII and reject X12 delimiters/controls; contacts/phone/instructions have separate length limits. See [stop data and migration behavior](stops.md).

Appointment booking/rescheduling body (strict fields; operations permission):

```json
{
  "expected_load_version": 1,
  "stop": "pickup",
  "start_local": "2026-10-15T09:00",
  "end_local": "2026-10-15T10:00",
  "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles",
  "disambiguation": "reject",
  "contact": "Facility scheduler",
  "confirmation_reference": "External booking reference",
  "note": "Facility and carrier confirmed the window directly"
}
```

`stop` is `pickup`, `delivery`, or a planned intermediate `stop_` identifier. Local times use minute precision. `disambiguation` defaults to `reject`; `earlier`/`later` explicitly choose a repeated daylight-saving time. Nonexistent local times always fail. Starts must match the plan's local stop date, the end is within 48 hours at/after the start, and active appointment starts must follow the full route order in UTC. Active windows extend carrier/driver qualification checks through their final local day. Rescheduling creates a replacement linked to its predecessor. Gate arrival/completed stops protect the original appointment baseline; cancel a booking before revising its stop details/date.

Gate record body:

  "stop": "pickup",
  "kind": "arrival",

Correction bodies use `expected_load_version`, `local_time`, `timezone`, optional `disambiguation`, `reference`, and `note`; stop/kind/appointment/tender identity derive from the original event. Original and correcting records remain. The known event sequence must stay chronological and actual times cannot exceed server time by more than five minutes. Workspace responses expose `appointments`, `stop_events`, and load `stop_execution: {has_overdue, pickup, delivery, ...intermediate_stop_ids}`. Each stop summary has its active appointment/current-attempt arrival/departure, `arrival_status` (`early`, `on_time`, `late`, `unscheduled`, or `unrecorded`), `late_minutes`, `overdue`, `dwell_minutes`, `dwell_open`, and `dwell_complete`. Completed stops missing a departure have unknown dwell; metrics do not create financial charges. Audit actors/proof/timezone resolution and all histories are retained. Imported-order writeback includes only operational window/actual timestamps through `trackingData.freight_stops`.

Workspace loads expose `pod_ready` for current finance review state. File content is excluded from the workspace response. Upload metadata includes an immutable digest, uploader, document version, and review history. See [document storage, evidence binding, and migration behavior](documents.md).

For paid-customer credits/refunds, `confirmation` is `{counterparty_contact, confirmation_reference, evidence_reference, note, document_id?}`. `customer_refund` bank entries require it; other bank directions reject it. Credit `issued_on` defaults to today and cannot precede invoice issuance or exceed today. Refund clearing and customer reversals cannot precede the latest invoice financial activity. See [workflow, exact request fields, totals, and integrity rules](customer-refunds.md).

Workspace bills include `activity_date` and totals `received_cents`, `credited_cents`, `refunded_cents`, signed `balance_cents`, positive `refund_due_cents`, and `remaining_creditable_cents`. Finance summary separates positive `receivable_cents` from `customer_credit_cents` and signed `net_receivable_cents`. Void cancellation invoices remain eligible refund targets when net funds are owed.

Staff workspace responses additionally expose `portal_offers`, `portal_decisions`, `carrier_submissions`, `customer_quote_publications` (excluding HTML), `customer_quote_decisions`, and `document_shares`. These are retained publication/decision/access histories; they are not the partner projection. Partner endpoints never return the staff workspace, raw source orders, bank/journal, private rate evidence, or other counterparties. `carrier`/`customer` credentials require server-owned `counterparty_id` and are denied every staff route, including generic file/document downloads. See [exact native-response shapes and source/qualification rules](partner-portal.md#api-and-persistence).

Workspace `rate_confirmations` include retained snapshots, original HTML digest, metadata version, handoffs/retractions/resolutions, `current`, and `basis_changed`; HTML itself is omitted and downloaded through the statement route. Handoff changes advance load versions and constrain proven-unsent withdrawal. Old/changed handoff review is reflected in load `tender_control.open_incidents` and existing custody-sensitive gates. See [carrier document workflow](carrier-rate-confirmations.md).

Workspace responses additionally expose `billing_profile`, `bills` (including totals and aging), `credits`, `cash_entries`, `journal`, and the `finance` summary. Settlements have their own `version` and `balance_cents`. Customer records optionally include `billing_address`; legacy updates that omit it preserve its current value.

Additional charges appear in `charges`. Loads expose `commercial: {buy, sell, margin_cents, pending_buy, pending_sell, buy_locked, sell_locked}`. Each side's basis is `{base_amount_cents, charges: [{charge_id, kind, description, amount_cents}], total_amount_cents}`. Raw load `buy_cents`/`sell_cents` remain the original base rates. Invoices and bill snapshots include an optional `agreement` basis; older snapshots without it retain their existing totals. Customer statement lines include only the sell basis. Settlements use the matched approved invoice amount.

Proposal/correction body:

```json
{
  "expected_load_version": 5,
  "side": "buy",
  "kind": "detention",
  "description": "Agreed additional loading service",
  "amount_cents": 13751,
  "evidence_reference": "RATE-123/DETENTION-1",
  "document_id": null,
  "corrects_id": null
}
```

`side` is `buy` or `sell`. Supported kinds are `detention`, `lumper`, `fuel`, `layover`, `extra_stop`, and `other`. Amounts are positive minor units in the shipment's currency, and base plus approved additions cannot exceed 100,000,000 minor units. The evidence reference identifies one active proposal/approval per load/side, case-insensitively. Optional stored files must belong to the same load/tenant. A correction requires a rejected/voided predecessor for the same assignment, counterparty, side, and reference, without a prior replacement. Original amounts and decisions are preserved.

Review body:

```json
{
  "expected_load_version": 6,
  "expected_version": 1,
  "decision": "approved",
  "counterparty_contact": "Carrier accounting representative",
  "confirmation_reference": "External agreement CASE-15",
  "note": "Reviewed the evidence and verified the exact additional amount"
}
```

Review decisions are `approved`/`rejected`. Contact/confirmation are required for approval; rejection requires a reason in `note`. A void body has the same version/contact/confirmation/note fields without `decision`. These shapes reject unknown fields, including supplied actors or statuses. Server identity is recorded. Approvals/voids increment the load/charge versions, re-audit carrier amounts without rewriting them, and refresh a customer draft's amount/basis/version when applicable. Pending proposals hold their side's posting. Supporting stored bytes are checked atomically at charge approval and financial posting; generic document rejection cannot invalidate an approved charge's source.

Accepted carrier ownership is required to propose a charge. Carrier additions retain their tender identity; retired proposals cannot affect replacements. Release/custody holds prevent approval, and approved additions prevent silent cancellation/re-planning/release. The original basis locks when carrier billing is approved/a settlement exists or a non-void customer invoice has issued. Use the separate carrier adjustment routes for actual later carrier documents. See [charge lifecycle](charges.md) and [carrier adjustments](payables.md).

  "document_id": null,

```

Only `finance.write` may mutate these records. The positive 1–100,000,000 minor-unit total, in the source shipment's currency, must exactly equal 1–100 unique positive target allocations, fit the source credit, and fit all target payables. The source is excluded from its targets, and every settlement must belong to the same carrier with current ownership, approved invoice, reviewed delivery evidence, and no release/custody hold. Reversal body:

```json
{
  "expected_version": 1,
  "expected_source_version": 4,
  "targets": [
    { "target_id": "other_prepared_settlement_id", "expected_version": 2 }

  "reversed_on": "2026-10-15",
  "counterparty_contact": "Carrier correction desk",

Each settlement exposes signed `credit_application_cents`, effective `balance_cents`, and `credit_application_earliest_date`. All affected settlement versions advance atomically, including when only the source credit is partially consumed. See [workflow and preview](carrier-credit-applications.md).

```json
{
  "expected_load_version": 8,
  "invoice_id": "original_approved_invoice_id",
  "kind": "supplemental_invoice",
  "number": "CARRIER-SUP-15",
  "document_amount_cents": 1251,
  "issued_on": "2026-10-15",
  "description": "Agreed additional unloading service",
  "evidence_reference": "Actual carrier document and agreement reference",
  "document_id": null,
  "carrier_document_id": null,
  "corrects_id": null
}
```

Kinds are `supplemental_invoice` (addition), `credit_memo` (reduction), and `invoice_revision` (replace the recognized total; derive only the difference). Amounts are integer minor units in the shipment's currency; a replacement total may be zero. Document numbers allow 1–200 characters without controls and normalize trimming/ASCII case. Drafts retain their recognized basis, carrier/tender, creator, optional file digest, and source. `carrier_document_id` binds the canonical number, amount magnitude, currency, and date. Negative 210 totals remain signed in the source and require explicit verified credit-memo classification; positive headers cannot establish credit designation. Active duplicate financial documents and branching/implicit corrections are rejected.

Review requires `{expected_load_version, expected_version, decision: "approved" or "rejected", counterparty_contact, confirmation_reference, note}`. Reversal requires the version/contact/reference/note fields plus `reversed_on`, without `decision`. Posting requires current ownership and reviewed delivery evidence; stored bytes are checked atomically. Stale revised-total bases require rejection/correction. Explicit corrections can repair classification while preserving the prior draft/posting and source identity. Reversal dates cannot precede posting or be in the future; credits/debit reversals cannot make the recognized invoice total negative.

Workspace responses additionally expose `carrier_documents` and `carrier_adjustments`. Additional 210 receipt returns `{finance_review: true, carrier_document_id, load_id}` without posting money. Its inbox status is `finance_review`; classification/dismissal becomes `finance_reviewed` while retaining original notification/event/history. Received documents stay `pending`/`allocated` until finance resolves them. Adjustment statuses are `draft`, `posted`, `rejected`, or `reversed`.

Settlement `amount_cents` remains original principal; `total_amount_cents` includes active posted differences. `balance_cents` is signed after net payouts/refunds; `credit_balance_cents` is its positive credit magnitude. Negative balances have status `credit_due`. The finance summary reports positive `prepared_payable_cents` and separate `carrier_credit_cents`. Load `commercial.total_buy_cents`, `carrier_adjustment_cents`, and margin include posted carrier differences while original agreement bases remain unchanged.

Bank direction `carrier_refund` uses credit-bearing settlement targets and positive allocations. Each amount must fit the current credit balance, share one carrier, and sum exactly to the actual cleared refund. Its date cannot precede the supporting credit document/reversal. Existing bank-reference/version/reversal/correction guards apply; the app records the refund without initiating one.

Tender history appears in `tenders`, `releases`, and `tender_incidents`. Each load exposes `tender_id` and `tender_control: {can_withdraw, release_pending, open_incidents}`. Tender attempts retain their carrier/plan snapshots and independent `shipment_reference`; use that reference as the carrier-facing `shipment_id`, including when tendering again to the same carrier. The freight load reference and source commerce identity remain stable. Outbox records expose `tender_id`, cumulative `total_attempts`, and persistent `transmission` (`not_started`, `attempted`, or legacy `unknown`). Resetting retry backoff does not erase transmission evidence.

Release confirmation, retention, and incident resolution require this strict body (unknown fields are rejected):

```json
{
  "expected_load_version": 4,
  "carrier_contact": "Carrier dispatcher name and contact",
  "confirmation_reference": "External conversation or case reference",
  "note": "What the carrier confirmed and how custody was checked"
}
```

The authenticated operations subject is recorded by the server. Requesting release pauses EDI handoffs and dispatch while retaining ownership. Confirmation cannot release freight after pickup, with unresolved carrier conflicts/financial documents, or while an HTTP handoff has a live lease. An expired handoff lease is fenced without claiming its previous request was unsent. See [carrier release and reconciliation](tenders.md).

Authenticated release negotiation uses these additional routes. All mutation bodies are strict; actor, carrier, tender, and disposition derive from the authenticated identity and stored request.

| Method | Route                                            | Permission and body                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/v1/release-requests/{id}/portal-publications`  | `operations.write`; `{expected_load_version, expected_previous_id?, message, respond_by}`; UTC RFC3339 deadline in the future and within seven days                                                     |
| POST   | `/v1/portal/releases/{publication_id}/response`  | `portal.carrier.release`; `{expected_load_version, document_sha256, decision: "release"\|"retain", contact, reference, note, no_custody?}`; release requires `no_custody: true`, retention must omit it |
| POST   | `/v1/release-responses/{id}/apply`               | `operations.write`; `{expected_load_version}`; applies original retained acknowledgement after all current checks                                                                                       |
| GET    | `/v1/portal/releases/{publication_id}/statement` | `portal.read`; exact original HTML/hash for its owning carrier only                                                                                                                                     |
| GET    | `/v1/release-publications/{id}/statement`        | Staff read; exact original HTML/hash                                                                                                                                                                    |

Staff workspace responses include `release_publications` without HTML and retained `release_responses` with source evidence hashes and separate application evidence. Carrier `GET /v1/portal` includes scoped `release_requests`: frozen snapshot/document hash, status, action eligibility, own response, and a current load version only while that exact assignment/request remains current. It excludes private operations reasons and replacement-carrier execution. A native positive acknowledgement held by a live lease/finance/custody review returns `outcome: "awaiting_operations"` and no application; it retains the assignment. Later application leaves the original carrier evidence unchanged. Expiry prevents both release response and application, while native retention can close an expired request. Publication/response/application require idempotency keys and version fences. See [workflow and hold semantics](tenders.md#authenticated-carrier-release).

| `accept` / `decline` | none                             | tendered; records manual carrier response                                                                                 |
| `dispatch`           | `driver_id`, `equipment_id`      | accepted                                                                                                                  |
| `pickup`             | none                             | dispatched                                                                                                                |
| `location`           | `location`                       | in_transit                                                                                                                |
| `deliver`            | `pod_reference` or `document_id` | in_transit                                                                                                                |
| `attach_pod`         | `pod_reference` or `document_id` | delivered; evidence cannot change after invoice approval/settlement                                                       |
| `exception`          | `note`                           | any open load                                                                                                             |
| `resolve`            | none                             | load with an exception                                                                                                    |
| `withdraw_tender`    | none                             | tendered; every associated handoff must be proven never attempted; returns to planned                                     |
| `cancel`             | none                             | planned, or tendered with proven never-attempted handoffs; other pre-pickup assignments require confirmed carrier release |

The normalized EDI envelope contains `event_id`, `event_type`, `occurred_at`, and `payload`. The payload must identify the tender attempt's `shipment_reference` as `shipment_id` and its snapshot `partner_id`; provided SCACs must match. An active legacy assignment retains its original load reference until released. An ambiguous load-reference fallback cannot select a new tender. See the integration runbook for the exact upstream callback and normalized-event distinction.

Signed callbacks return `{received: true, action: "queued", inbox_id, status, replayed}` **after** durable receipt, without contacting EDI in the callback request. The worker's separate `applied` outcome confirms the business transition committed. `pending`, `processing`, `retry`, `held`, `applied`, and `ignored` describe ordinary processing. `reconciliation_required` means authenticated historical carrier movement/invoice evidence was retained as a conflict without applying it to the replacement assignment. Operations incident resolution changes that item to `reconciled`; it does not post its invoice or replay physical movement. Retry is unavailable for this business reconciliation state. The original authenticated body, canonical event when available, processing result, and completed attempt history remain in the tenant workspace. Operator retry restarts the backoff cycle while retaining cumulative attempts and history.

For 214 tracking events, `events` is processed in document order. Its final `status_code` must match `latest_status`; absent `events` retains compatibility with a single normalized `latest_status`. A failure anywhere in a document rolls back the entire batch. Individual observations retain source date/time/location and document event identity in activity details; receipt time does not replace their original evidence. AG estimates do not move the physical last-reported location, and later repeated pickup/arrival observations do not regress a delivered shipment.

## Snapshot admission overload

Queued snapshot reads have per-process global/tenant count limits and a queue deadline. Exhaustion/expiry returns HTTP 503, `Retry-After: 1`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, and `error.code: "read_capacity_exceeded"`. No snapshot work starts for those requests. The gateway retains the response and retry hint; credential verification treats it as temporary unavailability and issues no session. Physical tracking commands avoid unnecessary source-read preflights, while tender/dispatch and other commitment workflows retain canonical source checks. See [settings, lifecycle, tests and limits](read-overload.md).

Known PostgreSQL lock/statement cancellation and pool acquisition expiry return HTTP 503 with the same retry/cache headers and `error.code: "database_temporarily_unavailable"`. Database I/O loss, a closed pool and explicit PostgreSQL connection/shutdown conditions return the same code with `message: "Database is temporarily unavailable. Check the original request before retrying."`. Protocol violations, decode failures and ordinary integrity errors retain storage-error behavior. These classifications do not retry operations or establish that a disconnected write failed to commit. Credential verification preserves this code without issuing a session or automatically retrying. Retain the original mutation key and exact body and use receipt-aware recovery; every HTTP 5xx response remains an uncertain browser save. See [runtime settings and recovery evidence](database-budgets.md).

`GET /v1/workspace` preserves complete approval evidence by default, including with `history=deferred`. Staff may opt into `X-Freight-Approval-Details: deferred` to omit only `entry_review_note`, `approval_note` and `evidence_reference` from each populated `approval_control.approval_evidence`. The seven decision/revision/actor/time fields remain. `complete` preserves the default; unsupported header values return 400. The header changes representation, never authorization. Workspace responses declare `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Vary: X-Freight-Approval-Details`.

The staff UI sends the optional compact header. A compatible preceding API ignores it and still supplies complete evidence, which remains directly usable without the new endpoint. Existing clients and older UIs receive the complete response by default. No write endpoint, financial policy, migration or stored format changes. This resource still materializes the complete tenant source; its response limit is not a database/decoding capacity qualification.

## TMS MCP adapter

The repository includes a local stdio MCP server at `mcp/src/index.mjs`. It uses the official MCP server SDK 2.3.1 and supports the 2026-07-28 protocol plus legacy 2025 clients. Its reviewed catalog covers all 126 protected API operations, including staff and partner reads, planning, procurement, execution, finance, integrations, save resolution, and original document/POD uploads. The unprotected health, metrics and signed webhook endpoints are outside this tool surface. The adapter delegates authorization, source/version checks and receipts to the same API as other clients.

Install with `npm --prefix mcp ci`, then configure a host using `mcp/client-config.example.json`. Point the command directly at Node 22 or later and `mcp/src/index.mjs`; stdout carries only MCP messages. Configure `FREIGHT_MCP_API_URL` as the backend API origin and exactly one of `FREIGHT_MCP_TOKEN_FILE` or `FREIGHT_MCP_TOKEN`. Prefer a private credential file; its contents are read afresh before each request. Use HTTPS outside loopback, or explicitly allow a trusted private HTTP network with `FREIGHT_MCP_ALLOW_HTTP=true`. TLS uses Node's normal verification and optional `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`. No credential, tenant, arbitrary URL or identity-header tool argument exists.

For Clerk, additionally set `FREIGHT_MCP_IDENTITY_MODE=clerk` and the fixed `FREIGHT_MCP_ORGANIZATION_ID=org_...`. Supply a current signed session JWT through the credential source. The API checks current membership/session status for every business request; the required Clerk header prevents fallback to a static credential. Token refresh may update the private file; changing organizations requires updating the configured binding and restarting the MCP process.

Four tools are exposed:

- `freight_catalog`: discover operation names, registered methods/paths, descriptions and 28 bundled request guides. Guides are available through `freight://guides/<name>` resources; they contain documentation rather than live records.
- `freight_read`: call a registered GET operation, with an entity `id` where applicable and literal string `query` values. Use paginated `load_catalog`, `operations_board` and `history_page` for bounded discovery. Original JSON is returned in `response.text`; binary content is base64. Preserve integer precision when interpreting JSON text.
- `freight_write`: supply a registered operation, original `idempotency_key`, and exact `body_json` object text. JSON is validated but never parsed and reserialized for forwarding, preserving original bytes and integer cents. Include the API's expected versions, source digests and genuine evidence. Supported original-save resolution uses operation `resolve_save` and the original `request_key`, canonical path/body and note described above.
- `freight_upload`: supply canonical `body_base64`, a plain `content_type`, original key, and the API's entity/query fields. The adapter retains the API's 10 MiB document limit; JSON writes retain its 1 MiB limit.

Results expose `ok`, `http_status` when received, original request metadata/digest and complete response bytes/digest. API 401/403/409/422/503 responses remain errors with their status and details. A missing complete response after dispatch is `unconfirmed` for writes: it may follow a real commit. The adapter never automatically retries, follows redirects, invents success or generates a replacement key. Retain the original tool arguments durably in the host before invoking a write, then explicitly replay that same original or use the resolver for a supported request. This adapter has no durable command journal, and the resolver supports its documented path set, not every API operation. Cancellation cannot undo an accepted request. A `not_sent` result identifies local rejection before dispatch. Document reads may append API download audit evidence; tool annotations are conservative hints, not authorization.

The default response budget is 16 MiB, configurable through `FREIGHT_MCP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` (1 KiB–64 MiB). Inbound MCP frames allow 32 MiB, including base64 overhead for the full document limit. Configure compatible client frame limits for large results; SDK qualification uses 64 MiB. Timeouts default to 30 seconds and may be set with `FREIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS` (1–120,000). An interrupted or over-budget write response remains unconfirmed. Returned business text and guides are data; they do not authorize further actions.

A nonroot container can be built with `docker build -t stateset-freight-mcp -f mcp/Dockerfile mcp`. It serves stdio, so launch it with an open stdin (`-i`) through a host. Pass credentials by protected file/environment, use a read-only filesystem and supply network access to the configured API. This is a process-scoped MCP connection; it does not commission a public MCP HTTP/OAuth service or configure an external host/account.

Native iCommerce connections use operator-configured credentials and tenant routing. See [iCommerce ownership, lifecycle and uncertain PATCH recovery](icommerce.md).


## Terminal financial and queue pages

`GET /v1/console` requires staff `workspace.read`. `/v1/access` advertises `features.console_catalog: true` when it is available. The authenticated principal determines the tenant; tenant, owner and other unknown query overrides are rejected. The endpoint is read-only and declares `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Required `view` is `billing`, `payables` or `integrations`. `limit` defaults to 50 and accepts 1–100. `q` is a trimmed, Unicode case-insensitive literal substring of exposed values (including amounts formatted in each record's currency), at most 200 normalized UTF-8 bytes. Search runs before paging and never searches omitted payloads, authentication or serialized field names.

Billing and Payables accept `balance=all|open|credits|zero|unknown`; Billing also accepts `overdue`. Classification uses signed integer cents, with positive balances open, negative balances credits, and overdue requiring a positive balance and positive reported overdue days. Missing values never become zero; financial arithmetic overflow fails the read. Queues accept `attention=true|false` and `direction=all|outbound|inbound`. Attention includes exactly retry, held and failed. Filters from another view are rejected, even if set to their defaults.

Responses include `tenant_id`, `view`, `limit`, `total` (all matching rows), `next_cursor` and arrays `bills`, `settlements`, `outbox`, `inbox`. Irrelevant arrays are empty. At most `limit` records are returned across all arrays combined. Financial `finance` cards always describe the entire workspace, independently of search, filter or page; `totals_scope` is `workspace`. Queue pages do not calculate financial totals. Bills omit customer contact/payment instructions and full commercial snapshots; queues omit payloads, upstream responses, callback bodies/authentication, histories and lease tokens. Recorded last-error text remains available as operational evidence and must not be used for secrets.

Opaque cursors accept at most 2048 bytes and bind the authenticated tenant/subject, normalized filters, page size and ordered matching identities. Financial rows sort by ID. Queues sort outbound first, then inbound, with direction-qualified IDs so equal raw IDs cannot collide. Membership changes invalidate the cursor; field changes that retain membership return fresh values. Cursors are navigation state, never authorization. Start at page one after a rejected cursor. Each page is a fresh read rather than a fixed snapshot across pages.

With migration 030 installed, PostgreSQL reads use a rebuildable console index. Warm pages fetch at most `limit + 1` projected rows through a keyset index; the extra row determines the next cursor. Balance, direction, attention and overdue equalities use fixed prepared statement shapes so PostgreSQL can plan them as indexed predicates. Exact counts, matching identity digests and literal substring search still scan matching projected candidates; they are not constant-cost or full-text/trigram searches. Original workspace payloads are not decoded on warm reads.

The first read after a canonical write, cache loss or UTC date rollover rebuilds all three projections under the original tenant row lock. This cold rebuild uses normal snapshot and workspace admission before acquiring a database connection. Canonical header/block triggers invalidate the projection in the source transaction, including writes from an already-running preceding binary. Rebuilds never rewrite original business records, receipts, versions or source timestamps. Financial arithmetic errors quarantine financial views without representing them as empty or blocking queue reads. Duplicate identities fail closed. Cancellation retains page, snapshot and workspace admission through the actual rebuild transaction's commit or rollback.

The projection expires on UTC date changes so overdue days, filters, search values and workspace totals are rebuilt together. A date change during a read causes retry rather than returning expired aging. Memory/demo stores retain the native projection implementation. Cursor version 2 hashes matching direction-qualified identities identically in memory and SQL; version-1 tokens are rejected and callers should restart at page one. Tokens still preserve fresh-field behavior when matching membership is unchanged.

Install migration 030 with the migration role before starting this API, then refresh runtime grants using the existing runbook. Stored business format 21 is unchanged. Older binaries cannot restart against the new exact migration ledger; existing compatible canonical writers invalidate the new read cache. This local implementation and query-plan qualification do not establish production capacity or operator acceptance.

### Terminal evidence previews

`GET /v1/loads/{id}/documents` requires `workspace.read`. The tenant comes from the authenticated principal. It returns `{load_id, documents, total}` with the newest 100 documents, ordered by upload time descending and ID ascending. Each item contains ID, load ID, filename, kind, content type, size, original SHA256, version and latest review status. Review notes, binary content and other loads are excluded. A missing shipment returns 404. `total` makes truncation explicit; use the web workspace for older evidence.

`GET /v1/documents/{id}/preview` uses the same staff permission and tenant boundary as the original download. The store verifies original length and SHA256 before rendering. PNG and JPEG are decoded with strict 8192-pixel dimension limits, a 16-megapixel ceiling and a 64 MiB decoded-buffer ceiling, then oriented from image metadata, resized to fit 960×960 without enlarging, and composited onto white. Only these two decoders are enabled. PDF, malformed and oversized images return 422; PDF originals remain available through the existing download route. One process-wide preview permit admits work without queuing; contention returns 503. Blocking decode retains its permit if the requesting connection is cancelled.

A successful preview has `Content-Type: application/vnd.stateset.rgb8` and exactly width×height×3 row-major RGB bytes. Headers `X-Preview-Width`, `X-Preview-Height`, `X-Content-SHA256`, `X-Source-SHA256`, `X-Document-ID` and `X-Load-ID` bind the bytes to the catalog item and original. Both new routes return `Cache-Control: private, no-store`; previews also return `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Previewing never approves a document, updates a load, or changes the original bytes. Clients must treat the derivative as a visual aid, retaining the original for evidence decisions.

# Cancellation fees

A cancelled shipment can still have a separately agreed truck-ordered-not-used charge or customer cancellation fee. Freight records that obligation without marking the freight delivered, fabricating POD, or posting the original transport buy/sell rates. [Carrier release](tenders.md) still establishes operational cancellation; a fee proposal never releases a carrier.

## Operational and finance workflow

1. Cancel an unassigned planned load, withdraw a proven-unsent offer, or request and record actual carrier-confirmed release. Picked-up freight cannot use this cancellation workflow. Resolve any late carrier custody/invoice incidents before fee decisions.
2. Open the cancelled shipment and select **Propose cancellation fee**. Choose customer charge or carrier cost, an explicit positive amount in the shipment's currency, description, and line-specific agreement reference. Attach an immutable shipment file or identify evidence held externally. Operations and finance can propose; a proposal posts no money.
3. A carrier cost must select the exact historical tender that was released with actual carrier confirmation. Its original carrier snapshot survives cancellation and subsequent changes to the directory. Multiple fee agreements can have independent targets, including fees involving different released carrier attempts; they do not restore carrier ownership. Customer agreements retain the proposing shipment customer's snapshot.
4. Finance opens **Freight audit → Cancellation fees** and selects **Review cancellation fee**. Verify the actual counterparty, agreement, and original file; record the contact, confirmation reference, and findings. Approval of a carrier cost requires the actual carrier invoice number and creates a prepared payable for that fee. Approval of a customer charge requires a new customer invoice number, due date at/after issuance, configured issuer, and an actual bill-to address in the proposal snapshot. It immediately issues that fee's frozen invoice. Rejection retains the proposal and decision without posting.
5. Download the customer cancellation invoice from the shipment or customer billing workspace. It identifies the shipment as cancelled, labels planned dates as planned, and itemizes only the agreed cancellation service. It omits carrier costs and internal contact/proof information. Recording issuance does not send the invoice.
6. Use **Bank reconciliation** for actual cleared receipts, payouts, and customer/carrier refunds. Each cancellation agreement has its own versioned target, so one fee cannot consume another's balance. Carrier payment can precede the cancelled shipment's planned pickup; the actual fee posting date is the earliest eligible date. Existing partial/batched allocation, counterparty, duplicate-bank-reference, reversal, and stale-version checks apply. Recording reconciliation does not send money.

The cancelled load's commercial totals use posted cancellation fees and active customer credits. Original buy/sell rates remain historical plan fields. Ordinary freight invoice approval and settlement still require delivery/POD; cancellation fees have their own agreement and journal source. Fee decisions do not generate EDI price/cancellation messages, commerce invoices, or tracking payloads containing finance data.

## Corrections and retained history

Finance can **Reverse cancellation fee** with actual counterparty confirmation, a reason/date, and current fee/load/target versions. The reversal appends opposite journal entries and preserves original invoices, amounts, proof, and bank allocations. Its effective date cannot precede posting or related bank/credit-application activity or be in the future.

- Reverse active customer credit notes before retracting a customer cancellation invoice. Preserve genuine receipts: retraction voids the invoice and exposes only net funds actually retained as a customer refund liability. Generic **Void invoice** is unavailable for fee invoices, because it would leave their agreement state inconsistent. Customer credits, including after payment with actual confirmation, remain available through normal billing; they reduce its receivable and commercial revenue. Reconcile an actual customer refund separately after the external return clears.
- Retracting an already paid carrier fee creates a negative balance on its original payable. Record an actual carrier refund, or a carrier-confirmed credit application to another eligible payable for that carrier. The original payout is retained. The application moves liability between its targets without posting expense or cash again.
- **Correct cancellation fee** creates a new proposal linked to the uncorrected rejected/reversed predecessor. It must retain shipment, side, counterparty, carrier attempt, and agreement reference. No implicit reuse or branching is allowed. Reapproval creates a new independent target; the old target and any credit/refund remain. A corrected carrier document may retain its actual invoice number only through that explicit reversed predecessor chain. Unrelated carrier invoices/adjustments and fee agreements cannot claim the same number for the same carrier. Customer invoice numbers remain unique, including void history.

Cleared customer funds are not automatically refunded or transferred to a replacement invoice. Reverse an erroneous reconciliation only when supported by the actual bank evidence. Use [customer refund reconciliation](customer-refunds.md) for actual returns; external refund execution and customer credit reassignment remain separate workflows; do not reverse a genuine receipt merely to force a correction through.

## Evidence, security, and integrations

Proposals retain creator/time and the original amount, counterparty snapshot, carrier tender, and evidence digest. Finance decisions and reversals record the authenticated subject. Stored evidence must belong to this tenant/load and cannot already be rejected. Fee approval verifies its exact bytes inside the business transaction. Cash posting against a cancellation target and carrier credit applications also verify supporting bytes. Corruption rolls back the entire mutation, including new targets, journals, audit, correction pointers, and idempotency receipts. A file supporting retained posted cancellation history cannot subsequently be rejected; its history and original bytes remain available.

`charges.write` permits proposals. `finance.write` permits decisions/reversals and existing bank/billing operations. Read access can inspect/download existing records; integration credentials cannot assert a human agreement. Body-supplied identities, amounts outside the supported positive range, wrong-load proof, unconfirmed/wrong carrier attempts, stale versions, and unexpected fields fail before mutation.

Late signed 210s against a released tender continue to enter the existing historical-carrier reconciliation queue. A 210 total does not establish cancellation eligibility or auto-approve a fee. Investigate and retain the original event/document, resolve the carrier incident with actual findings, then record the verified fee and invoice evidence. The existing gateway supports original 204 offers; partner cancellation/change messages remain commissioning work. No sibling repository is modified.

Cancellation persistence was introduced in [storage format 2](storage.md), added by migration `004_cancellation_fees.sql`. It upgrades format 1 atomically, retains prior migration checksums/history and existing business fields, and prevents a previous API from rewriting away cancellation records.

## API

- `POST /v1/loads/{id}/cancellation-fees`: `{expected_load_version, side: "buy"|"sell", tender_id?, amount_cents, description, evidence_reference, document_id?, corrects_id?}`. Carrier side requires its released tender; customer side must omit/null the tender.
- `POST /v1/cancellation-fees/{id}/review`: `{expected_load_version, expected_version, decision: "approve"|"reject", counterparty_contact, confirmation_reference, note, number?, due_date?}`. Approval requires an actual invoice number; only customer approval includes a due date.
- `POST /v1/cancellation-fees/{id}/reverse`: `{expected_load_version, expected_version, expected_target_version, reversed_on, counterparty_contact, confirmation_reference, note}`.

All mutations require `Idempotency-Key`. Workspace responses include `cancellation_fees` with retained decisions/correction links and existing `bills`/`settlements` with their normal balances/versions. Requesting the same successful command again replays its response without another target or posting.

Local qualification uses independently expected 25,001-cent carrier and 37,501-cent customer fees: actual payments leave zero balances and 12,500 cents of net cash movement. A retracted paid 25,001-cent fee followed by a corrected 15,001-cent fee reconciles to 15,001 cents of cost/net cash without changing the original payout/principal. A separate 10,000-cent cancelled payable consumes only 10,000 of an agreed 25,001-cent carrier credit, leaving 15,001 for an actual refund. Tests also inspect strict guards, erroneous receipt/credit correction and paid customer retraction retaining genuine receipts with a refund limited to actual funds received, invoice escaping, file corruption, competing PostgreSQL decisions/allocations, reconnect, role denial, production browser operation, and mobile controls. All records are synthetic; no live carrier agreement or bank transfer is represented as verified by these fixtures.

# Carrier contract rates and procurement

These lane agreements price two-endpoint shipments. A [multi-stop route](multi-stop.md) is explicitly ineligible even when its origin, destination, equipment, dates, and limits match. Record an actual carrier offer covering the full route instead; an extra-stop charge does not silently expand a lane agreement's scope.

In **Quotes**, **Carrier lane agreements** retains reusable, staff-reviewed external pricing. A lane agreement is separate from available capacity, a carrier tender, customer acceptance, and financial posting. The catalogue supports inclusive flat rates in one [currency](multi-currency.md) per agreement (USD by default) for full truckload shipments, exact directed US/Canadian postal lanes, equipment, optional customer scope, pickup/delivery period, and maximum declared weight/mileage.

## Record and maintain the agreement

1. Inspect the original carrier agreement. Choose **Record carrier agreement** and select the actual carrier, agreement number, customer scope, directed postal lane, equipment, limits, inclusive price, date range, and original terms. Record the actual carrier contact, external source reference, substantive private findings, and revision reason. Acknowledge the reviewed evidence and save. This retains a named operator's attestation; it does not independently verify a carrier signature or communicate acceptance.
2. **Original terms and revision history** preserves each frozen carrier/customer snapshot, normalized scope, amount, terms, source evidence, actor/time, original HTML, and SHA-256 hashes. **Download agreement revision** returns those exact original recorded bytes. This is Freight's record of the reviewed external agreement, not an uploaded original signed contract. The original source remains identified by its external reference.
3. **Revise carrier agreement** creates a new immutable revision under the same agreement number/carrier, with fresh external evidence and the reviewed agreement version. Changing the carrier or agreement number requires a separate agreement. Duplicate carrier/number pairs are rejected, including case variants.
4. **Withdraw for new sourcing** records actual carrier evidence and stops further sourcing. The original revisions, their documents, independently confirmed offers, bookings, tenders, and invoices remain. Withdrawal is final for that catalogue record; a new agreement needs its own number. No existing financial obligation is reversed.

The source digest binds the agreement ID, revision, carrier/customer snapshots, exact rate terms, original evidence, reason, actor, and time. Hash and reproducible HTML checks reject corruption. The agreement's current version and original revision digest are required when sourcing; background refresh cannot substitute a newly revised price into an open reviewed form.

## Evaluate and confirm capacity

Open a quote and choose **Find contract rates**. Every agreement is compared on the server against that quote's current plan; inapplicable candidates display reasons. Nothing automatically selects the cheapest carrier or books capacity.

- Country, state/province, and postal codes must match the exact origin-to-destination direction. Case/spacing are normalized, as are US ZIP9 separators. ZIP5 does **not** cover ZIP9; reverse lanes, wildcard/zone searches, and geographic/routing inference are not implemented.
- The shipment must be FTL with matching equipment, within the stated weight and mileage limits, and in the agreement's customer scope. Both pickup and delivery must fall within the inclusive agreement dates. Limits use the declared quote plan; this does not calculate a routed mileage or independently measure freight weight.
- The carrier's current SCAC/EDI partner identity must match the recorded revision, its equipment must qualify, and its insurance must cover delivery and the current date. Expired or withdrawn rates cannot be newly sourced.
- Draft quotes can receive offers. A booked shipment can use replacement procurement only when safely returned to planning and unassigned. The existing custody, financial, load-version, source-review, and fresh canonical Sync controls apply at commitment.

Inspect the exact agreement, then **Confirm capacity at this rate**. The form freezes the selected agreement/version/hash and quote/load versions. Record current carrier capacity contact, reference, findings, and expiry, then acknowledge that capacity and the exact inclusive rate were confirmed. The request cannot provide a caller-selected price, carrier, actor, or rate-source snapshot: those derive from the stored agreement and authenticated operations identity.

Sourcing records a normal carrier offer plus its exact agreement revision/digest. Customer quote issuance, actual customer acceptance, booking, tender, carrier acceptance, and delivery remain separate. Customer issuance cannot outlive the selected capacity offer. Revising or withdrawing the reusable agreement later does not rewrite a separately confirmed price/capacity offer; that offer retains its own expiry, withdrawal, reconfirmation, qualification, and custody controls. Every subsequent commitment verifies the original source terms/hash and exact offer price. Contract replacement procurement changes only the safely unassigned buy agreement and retains the accepted customer sell agreement and previous awards.

These rates are inclusive base prices. Agreement terms must accurately describe the external commitment. Fuel-index formulas, tariff classes, per-mile/per-weight arithmetic, spot-market feeds, automatic accessorials, customer sell-side contracts, and capacity reservation require additional workflows. Ordinary documented additions still use [charge proposals and finance review](charges.md).

## Access and persistence

Creation, revision, withdrawal, capacity attestation, and replacement procurement require `operations.write`. All tenant staff readers can inspect/download the private catalogue. Carrier/customer portal roles cannot reach these staff routes and never receive the catalogue, private contract terms, or source evidence through portal projections. Native customer acceptance does not disclose the carrier's buy contract. Published carrier/customer documents retain their established separate scopes.

Migration `015_carrier_contracts.sql` advances format 12 to **13**, preserving previous business records, file bytes, timestamps, and migration history. It adds `carrier_contracts`; carrier offers have optional retained `rate_source`. Old writers are fenced before they can discard the catalogue or procurement provenance. See [upgrade/rollback](storage.md).

## API

All writes require `Idempotency-Key` and strict bodies. UTC/RFC3339 applies to capacity expiry; agreement dates use `YYYY-MM-DD`.

| Method | Route | Body or result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/v1/carrier-contracts` | `{number, carrier_id, rate, contact, reference, note, reason}` |
| POST | `/v1/carrier-contracts/{id}/revise` | Same fields plus `expected_version`; number/carrier fixed |
| POST | `/v1/carrier-contracts/{id}/withdraw` | `{expected_version, contact, reference, note}` |
| GET | `/v1/carrier-contracts/{id}/statement?revision=N` | Exact recorded HTML/hash, attachment/no-store protections; omit revision for current |
| GET | `/v1/quotes/{id}/contract-rates` | Quote/version, offer/replacement context, current booked load version, candidates with applicability/reasons and original digest |
| POST | `/v1/quotes/{id}/contract-offers` | `{expected_version, agreement_id, expected_rate_version, revision_sha256, valid_until, contact, reference, note}` |
| POST | `/v1/quotes/{id}/contract-reprocure` | Same sourcing fields plus `expected_load_version, reason`; fresh source verification before an imported commitment |

`rate` contains `{customer_id?, origin, destination, equipment, max_weight_lbs, max_miles, effective_from, effective_through, amount_cents, terms}`. Lane points are `{country, state, postal_code}`. Missing/null customer scope means all customers. Supported limits are 1–80,000 lbs and 1–10,000 miles; price is 1–100,000,000 integer minor units in the agreement's currency. The period must end today or later and within three years. Terms require 1–2,000 characters; other human evidence fields require 1–200. Staff workspace responses include revision metadata without HTML, original evidence, withdrawal history, and offer/award `rate_source` pointers.

## Verified evidence

Six Rust tests exercise exact 125,001-cent sourcing and independent capacity, applicability and current qualification, stale/forged requests, corruption before issuance/tender, retained old terms after a new 130,001-cent revision/withdrawal, staff-only original downloads, and safe replacement while preserving 150,001-cent customer pricing. PostgreSQL tests race competing uses and revision/withdrawal against sourcing, reject corrupt HTML/source evidence transactionally, reuse failed keys only after restoration, and retain original selections/actor/bytes after reconnect across four owned tenants. Migration qualification includes the previous format-12 database/history.

The actual sibling codec builds a real 204 from a contract-sourced quoted Sync import. Actual-service runtime qualification sources a contract on the canonical Sync shipment, then retains its identity through native customer acceptance, booking, real EDI tender/callbacks, native carrier execution/POD, reviewed finance, safe cancellation, and restart.
