# Shipment documents and delivery evidence

Carriers can submit original receiver POD through the [scoped partner portal](partner-portal.md#report-movement-and-submit-pod) after delivery. That path atomically stores and attaches the file with authenticated carrier/tender provenance and an unreviewed status. Carrier submission grants neither finance review nor generic staff-file access. Rejected originals remain retained when a replacement is submitted.

Open a shipment and use Shipment documents to retain a PDF, JPEG, or PNG. Supported kinds are POD, bill of lading, rate confirmation, carrier invoice, and other. Files may contain up to 10 MiB. Filenames, declared media type, and basic format signatures must agree. The application stores the original bytes unchanged and computes their SHA-256 digest. These checks identify and preserve the file; they do not establish signature authenticity.

In real workspaces, `freight_document_content` stores bytes in PostgreSQL, separately from workspace JSON. An upload commits its bytes, metadata, audit entry, and idempotency receipt in the same transaction. Repeating the same upload key returns the original document. A changed filename, kind, media type, or content under that key conflicts. Concurrent requests from different API replicas cannot create duplicate files under one key. Demo bytes live in memory and reset with the API, just like demo records.

All tenant staff roles can download documents belonging to their tenant. Downloads check the stored byte length and digest, return attachments with `nosniff`, and disable caching. File names support Unicode. Foreign tenant IDs return 404 even when the caller knows the document ID. Workspace responses include metadata and review history, never file bytes. Both the web gateway and API bound upload sizes before retaining the full body.

Operations and finance can upload files. Only finance/admin can review them. Reviews require an explicit accepted/rejected decision, a note, and the expected document version. The server records the authenticated subject and timestamp. Review history is append-only; stale concurrent decisions conflict. Files cannot be overwritten or deleted through the API. Upload a new document when a carrier supplies replacement evidence.

For a stored POD, select the document when confirming delivery, or choose Use as POD after a 214 has confirmed delivery. The file must belong to that load, have kind `pod`, and not be rejected. It may await finance review; the shipment remains delivered while invoice approval stays blocked. A D1 alone still supplies no POD.

For evidence held externally, enter the actual reference and have finance use Review external POD. Finance must inspect that external evidence and record the review; the application does not fetch arbitrary external URLs. Reviews bind to the exact reference. Replacing it clears the current review and requires a new decision. Earlier decisions remain in the shipment audit.

Carrier invoice approval, customer invoice issuance, and settlement preparation require delivered status and accepted evidence; carrier approval also requires matched amounts. For a stored POD, each new approval/issuance/settlement also checks the original bytes inside the database transaction. Missing or altered bytes abort the entire mutation, including audit, journal, and idempotency writes. Restoring the original bytes allows the original failed request key to succeed. Once customer billing is issued, a carrier invoice approved, or a settlement prepared, its POD cannot be replaced or rejected. A later dispute requires an explicit finance reconciliation workflow; it cannot silently invalidate previously approved evidence.

Existing external references load without automatic acceptance. Previously approved invoices remain historical records; new approval/settlement requests require the explicit review. Synthetic demo deliveries contain clearly marked sample reviews.

Back up the whole freight database/schema together, including `freight_workspaces`, `freight_document_content`, the migration history, the format registry, and its guard function/trigger. Follow the [storage deployment and rollback procedure](storage.md). Apply database encryption, backup access, retention, and capacity policies appropriate to shipment evidence. This implementation uses PostgreSQL storage; external object-storage, automated signature verification, and document deletion/retention workflows are not configured.

Additional freight charges can bind an immutable supporting file to their proposal's original SHA-256 digest. Finance approval of that charge records its own review and counterparty confirmation; POD review remains separate. Charge approval verifies its stored bytes transactionally, and the relevant invoice issuance/approval/settlement checks those files again. Generic file rejection is blocked while an approved charge depends on it. [Charge evidence and posting locks](charges.md).

Carrier payable adjustment drafts likewise bind optional supporting files to their original digest. Posting checks that file, POD, and original charge evidence inside the tenant transaction. Settlement preparation rechecks active posted adjustment files. A posted adjustment's file cannot be rejected until the posting is reversed. Original approval and reversal confirmations remain separately readable. Canonical additional 210 events retain their original authenticated inbox evidence even when finance records a correction or dismissal.

Customer supplements also capture their optional agreement file's original digest. Issuance verifies those bytes in the same transaction as its receivable/journal/audit/receipt. A generic rejection cannot invalidate an issued non-void supplement's agreement file. Void/reconcile that invoice before rejecting its evidence. [Supplement billing](customer-supplements.md).

## Share original files with partners

Staff can publish an exact stored file to a named customer or carrier through **Shipment documents → Share file with partner**. The partner opens `/portal` and sees **Shared shipment files**. No file is automatically made available by belonging to a shipment or by being uploaded/attached as POD. Shared access remains authenticated; there is no public URL or browser-selected tenant/role.

1. Inspect the original file and filename. Select the exact customer account or carrier tender. Carrier options identify the actual carrier, tender sequence/status, and shipment reference; historical tenders can receive their own file after release. Existing legacy assignments are adopted with their retained identity and uncertain transmission history before creating a carrier grant.
2. Enter a message for the recipient and a separate private content-review note. Acknowledge that the original bytes and filename are appropriate for this recipient, then **Publish file access**. Publication checks the current load/document versions, freezes file metadata/hash and recipient/tender identity, and verifies the original stored bytes in the same transaction as its audit and receipt. Repeating the same command key replays its original result; changed requests conflict. Content review is a named staff decision; the application does not classify or redact PDF/image contents.
3. Only that counterparty sees the frozen filename, shipment reference, kind, size, hash, recipient message, current file review status, and access state. Staff review/revocation notes, financial totals, master data, and other parties' grants remain private. The partner downloads the exact immutable bytes with attachment/no-store/nosniff protections and the original SHA-256. Earlier explicitly shared files remain scoped to their original recipient/tender; they do not reveal a replacement carrier/customer's plan, price, location, or version.
4. **Partner file access** retains grants, private review notes, revocations, and download authorizations. **Revoke file access** stops future authorization under that grant and retains its original record. A new sharing decision after revocation requires the latest predecessor ID and creates a new grant; it does not reactivate the old URL. Operations, finance, and administrators can revoke access, including a mistaken financial-file disclosure. Revocation leaves the original file and all finance/POD evidence unchanged. Copies already downloaded, a carrier's own uploaded POD, and separately published rate/quote/invoice documents are independent of this grant.

Operations/finance/admin may share ordinary shipment files. A stored `carrier_invoice` or `rate_confirmation` file can be shared only with a carrier, and creation additionally requires finance/admin authority. Customer financial documents use the issued invoice/quote portal paths. The file's declared kind enforces this rule; staff must still inspect actual contents and filenames. Rejected files cannot receive new grants; rejection also holds downloads under existing grants without deleting their history. A later accepted review can restore access only under a grant that has not been revoked. Review status conveys the existing evidence decision, not automatic invoice approval or signature certification.

Publishing a file to a carrier is communication of that **exact tender**, even before a recorded download or an EDI attempt. Proven-unsent withdrawal therefore becomes unavailable. Revoking the grant cannot prove that instructions were never seen and cannot restore unsent status; obtain actual carrier release or record an actual decline. Sharing a customer's file or an old carrier tender's file does not communicate a replacement tender. File publication itself never accepts/tenders/dispatches freight, changes a commerce order, reviews POD, or posts a payment.

An open sharing form freezes the reviewed recipient identity, tender/history, original document version, and load version. Background refresh cannot silently substitute a new customer/carrier or raise its submitted version. If the shipment changes while the form is open, submission fails with a conflict and staff must reopen and review current details. This protects the actual disclosure decision as well as the stored grant.

### Authorization and revocation ordering

A partner download locks the tenant aggregate, checks the live principal and exact grant, checks original metadata/hash/bytes, records an authorization, and commits before releasing bytes. Revocation uses the same tenant lock. If revocation commits first, the download is denied; an authorization committed earlier can finish sending its already-authorized bytes. Missing/corrupt content rolls back the authorization and its audit. Records say **download authorized**; they do not establish network receipt, reading, or acceptance. No authorization is logged for a denied counterparty, rejected/revoked file, or failed integrity check.

### Sharing API and persistence

- Staff `POST /v1/documents/{document_id}/shares` under `documents.write`: `{expected_load_version, expected_document_version, audience: "customer"|"carrier", carrier_tender_id?, expected_previous_id?, message, review_note, acknowledge_content: true}`. Messages/notes require 1–200 characters. Customer identity comes from the current shipment; carrier identity comes from the selected exact tender. Omitting a carrier tender selects/adopts its current assignment. Clients cannot choose the counterparty, actor, role, content hash, file metadata, or access status.
- Staff `POST /v1/document-shares/{share_id}/revoke`: `{expected_version, note}` under `documents.write`. All business writes require `Idempotency-Key`; revocation remains available even when original bytes are corrupt.
- Partner `GET /v1/portal/files/{share_id}/content`: exact scoped bytes and a fresh live authorization; generic staff document IDs cannot be used as share IDs. Every successful authorization is audited; GET does not replay a cached business receipt or require an idempotency key.
- `GET /v1/portal` adds explicit `files` projections. Revoked/held entries retain their original descriptive metadata and access status but have no functioning download. Staff workspace responses add complete `document_shares` history, including private notes and authorizations.

Migration `013_document_sharing.sql` advances format 10 to **11**, preserving earlier records/files/history and fencing writers that could discard grants or ignore their custody effects. [Storage deployment and rollback](storage.md) covers upgrades. Qualification checks scope, forged input/role denial, financial-file rules, exact bytes, replay, private notes, revocation/resharing, rejection, legacy adoption, and historical tender isolation. PostgreSQL checks corruption rollback, competing grants, and a download racing revocation with retained authorization ordering. Browser qualification exercises the real staff and mobile partner flows. The actual EDI/Sync runtime also shares and revokes carrier-submitted POD without invalidating reviewed finance evidence.

See [API endpoints](api.md) and [role grants](access.md).

Carrier credit applications bind an optional file on their source shipment to its original digest. Application posting checks that file plus stored POD, approved original charges, and active carrier-adjustment files on the source and every target inside one tenant transaction. A corrupt target file cannot leave a partial allocation on the source. Active application evidence cannot be generically rejected until its application is reversed. Reversal remains available to unwind a mistaken allocation while retaining the original evidence and fresh carrier retraction proof. [Credit application workflow](carrier-credit-applications.md).

# Shared shipment execution timeline

Shipment details, current carrier offers, and customer shipments now show the same route-ordered actual observations. Expand **Execution timeline** to inspect each stop's gate arrival, actual pickup/delivery service, and gate departure. Missing times remain unrecorded. The timeline does not estimate travel, derive an ETA, fill missing gates, or infer service from arrival.

## One chronology across evidence sources

Known actual times follow origin arrival → origin pickup → origin departure → each intermediate arrival/service/departure → final arrival → final delivery → final departure. Origin/final service times come only from applied native carrier pickup/delivery reports; intermediate service times come from their immutable confirmations. Gate times use the original timezone-qualified observations and current explicit corrections.

Previously the gate sequence and service sequence were checked independently. Both sequences could be individually valid while contradicting one another across stops. The shared validator now checks the combined route before committing a new gate, service confirmation, correction, or applied native pickup/delivery. Its error identifies both conflicting stop numbers, observation kinds, and actual UTC times. Rejection changes no load version, evidence, audit, queue, or idempotency receipt.

Older native observations retained as `stale_ignored` remain in the carrier's original history but do not redefine an applied pickup/delivery milestone or constrain a later service correction. Delayed native evidence that actually advances shipment status still participates in chronology checks. Raw EDI observations retain their existing lifecycle behavior. EDI processing/receipt timestamps are not silently converted into timezone-qualified stop times.

## Repair existing conflicts without losing history

Reading an older inconsistent shipment exposes the original observations, conflict pairs, and a route attention item. It does not rewrite history or invent a corrected time. Correct original gate/service evidence through the existing operations controls, with actual supporting findings and the current load version. Each correction retains its predecessor.

When independent historical conflicts exist, one correction can repair one conflict while others remain visible. It cannot introduce a new conflict or leave its own corrected observation contradictory. Finance stays held until the known timeline is consistent, every required intermediate service is confirmed, and consolidated POD is finance-reviewed. Existing posted-evidence locks remain effective.

Applied native pickup/delivery times can now be repaired through [reviewed movement corrections](movement-corrections.md). The original authenticated report remains unchanged; a source-bound correction supplies the effective actual time. Raw EDI documents, location reports, physical status retractions, and retired assignments remain outside this workflow. Do not change correct gate/service times merely to force consistency.

The current tender scopes the view. Retired observations do not constrain or expose a replacement assignment. Staff see original evidence references and actors. Carrier/customer projections share operational kinds/times and facility order while omitting staff references, notes, and identities. A carrier's separate own-submission history remains available under its existing scope.

## Finance and Sync

Chronology consistency participates in delivery evidence readiness: carrier invoice approval, settlement preparation, and customer billing cannot proceed on conflicting execution times. Existing postings remain; this does not reverse or invent a payment.

Ordered Sync tracking adds `trackingData.freight_execution_consistent`. A final-delivery payload with a false flag stays `local_only`. The worker also checks current chronology for older final-delivery payloads without the flag, and rechecks its hold under the tenant lock. Original payloads and any previous transmission attempt remain recorded; Retry cannot force `local_only` payloads upstream. A later consistent correction enqueues a fresh snapshot, allowing final tracking on the original order UUID. In-transit physical tracking remains independent of final-delivery approval.

The marker is Freight metadata in Sync's raw tracking JSON. Canonical typed tracking continues exposing supported public fields such as tracking number and estimated delivery. No sibling repository is changed.

## Persistence and verification

Existing operations permissions govern gate/service and reviewed native time corrections; current carrier scope governs native movement reporting. The timeline itself is derived; the [native correction endpoint](movement-corrections.md#atomic-source-bound-correction) appends separately retained evidence. `GET /v1/workspace` adds each load's `execution_timeline: {consistent, evidence_valid, record_count, conflicts, stops}`. Partner responses add a public projection. Missing observations do not become stored records.

Migration 017 introduced the chronology fence in format 15; format 16 additionally retains native movement corrections and fences workers that ignore effective corrected times. Current format 17 retains operations ownership/follow-up history and source-derived recovery. These upgrades preserve business fields, timestamps, original documents, and migration history. Inconsistent history remains available for explicit repair rather than being normalized during migration.

# Freight finance

Freight audit now contains four workspaces: Carrier audit, Customer billing, Bank reconciliation, and Journal. All amounts are integer minor units in their shipment's [currency](multi-currency.md) (USD by default). Finance/admin credentials can change these records; other tenant staff can read them and download their tenant's statements and journal exports. The separate [load-board CSV](load-exports.md) preserves signed commercial amounts as numeric decimals, including negative margins and credits; it does not post accounting entries.

Staff workspace responses build one borrowed financial index per immutable snapshot. Cash allocations, credits, approved invoices, adjustments, cancellation obligations, recognition history and activity dates are selected without repeatedly scanning the complete tenant history for every bill and settlement. Original order and first-match rules remain intact; the index is discarded before returning the response and never becomes write authority. Display arithmetic refuses unrepresentable signed credits, refunds and account balances with a checked error.

## Customer billing

Configure Billing identity with your issuing legal name, address, billing contact, and payment instructions. The [reviewed identity editor](billing-identity-review.md) preserves the version and verified tenant/operator that opened the form, so a background refresh cannot silently overwrite another operator’s legal or payment details. A real workspace starts without these details. Synthetic demo identity is explicitly labeled. Add the customer's bill-to address in its master record or supply the address on the invoice draft.

Create a draft for a delivered load. The amount comes from the agreed inclusive base sell rate plus separately approved customer additions, never a browser-supplied total. One non-void original customer invoice is allowed per load. Numbers are normalized to uppercase, remain unique, and cannot be reused after voiding. Drafts can change number, due date, and bill-to address with an expected version. Approval/voiding of a customer addition refreshes the original draft basis and increments its version; pending customer proposals hold issuance. [Charge proposals and agreement evidence](charges.md).

Issuance requires delivered status, accepted POD evidence, a billing issuer, and a bill-to address. Stored POD bytes are checked inside the same database transaction. The invoice freezes its customer, issuer/payment instructions, bill-to address, shipment, source load version, currency, and sell amount. Later master-data/profile changes do not alter it. Its posting debits accounts receivable and credits freight revenue. Issuance does not send a message or establish customer receipt.

Download an HTML invoice to inspect, print, save as PDF, or pass to your billing process. It includes the agreed sell amount, credits, reconciled receipts/refunds, and outstanding balance; carrier buy cost, margin, internal review notes, and other customers' information are excluded. Draft/void documents are marked. Dynamic text is escaped, and downloads use attachment/no-store/nosniff protections.

Credit notes reduce the issued invoice amount with an explicit number, reason, and actual issue date. They debit freight revenue and credit accounts receivable. Total active credits cannot exceed the original amount, including after payment. A credit reducing received funds requires actual customer confirmation/evidence; the resulting negative receivable is a customer refund liability. Record an actual external return separately using bank direction `customer_refund`. Reverse an erroneous credit with an appended opposite posting; current invoice versions are required after refund history, and actual receipts/refunds remain. Ordinary invoice voiding requires zero net funds retained and no active credits. Voiding an issued invoice reverses its issuance journal; a void draft has no journal posting. [Paid-customer credit/refund workflow and correction rules](customer-refunds.md).

The UI shows original received, credited, refunded, and outstanding amounts separately, plus days past due for positive debt. Paid status means the invoice's net amount is covered by recorded net external receipts and credits. Fully credited invoices with no net receipts are labeled `credited`. Negative balances have status `credit_due`, except retracted invoices retain `void`. The summary separates positive receivables from `customer_credit_cents`; `net_receivable_cents` is signed. The platform records staff's external bank evidence; it does not independently verify a bank balance.

After original issuance, use **Draft supplement** on that original invoice to bill an additional amount supported by an actual customer agreement. Each supplement has its own number, due date, agreement/contact/confirmation, optional immutable supporting file, issuance, credits, and bank allocations. Its customer and shipment come from the frozen original; it does not repeat the original total. Issuance checks delivery and stored agreement bytes, posts separate receivable/revenue, and retains the original snapshot and payment history. Duplicate agreement references and implicit/branching corrections fail. Active supplements protect their original invoice from voiding. Load totals include issued non-void supplements and subtract active customer credit notes. [Supplement workflow, correction rules, and preview](customer-supplements.md).

## Carrier liabilities

Real workspaces require two named finance subjects for primary carrier invoice approval. **Review entry** records the actual carrier invoice reference and substantive findings against the displayed revision; **Approve** requires a different named finance subject and independent findings. Anyone who entered, corrected, classified a canonical revision, or reviewed that invoice's entry is excluded from approving it, including administrators and rotated credentials with the same subject. Legacy credential fingerprints and automated/system identities cannot perform these reviews. Configure stable scoped subjects or use staff sign-in, with at least two authorized people.

The review revision binds the invoice, current load version/assignment, retained entry/correction event identities, and the attached POD's current metadata and reviews. A stored-file review invalidates it even when the load version does not advance. Corrections back to the same amount still require a fresh entry review. Workspace and deferred-history responses include per-invoice `approval_control` with the revision, review subject, state, and allowed next action. The open review form retains its original revision. Server checks occur inside the same tenant transaction as posting and the receipt. Old approved records remain historical decisions; exact original receipts still replay without reinterpretation. Legacy unapproved invoices need an explicit current entry review; that attestation does not invent a historical creator or independently authenticate the carrier's document.

For an approved carrier invoice, **View approval** shows the recorded entry reviewer and independent approver, their original times with the viewer’s timezone, the carrier invoice evidence reference, and both sets of findings. It follows the exact `entry_review_id` and revision retained with the decision; approval itself changes the current invoice revision, and later POD/load updates do not erase or replace the original decision. The view is read-only and closes with Escape while returning focus to its link. By default, full and history-deferred API responses expose the same complete `approval_evidence`; the current action revision remains separate.

Approving a matched carrier invoice recognizes freight expense and carrier payable. Preparing its settlement does not post the same liability twice. Existing approved invoices from older snapshots are recognized once when their first settlement is prepared; this is an opening payable at the preparation date, not a reconstruction of historical books.

Settlements keep the matched approved invoice amount (original buy plus approved carrier additions) and a version. Their status moves between `prepared`, `partially_reconciled`, and `reconciled` as external payouts are recorded or reversed. Carrier invoices retain their approved state; a bank record is a separate entity. Pending carrier proposals hold invoice approval. Additional agreement approval re-audits an unposted invoice without altering its received amount. No transfer is initiated by approval, preparation, or reconciliation.

After primary approval, [carrier payable adjustments](payables.md) record actual supplemental invoices, replacement totals, and credit memos as separate drafts/postings. The original invoice and settlement principal stay fixed; effective settlement totals and versions include active posted differences. Credits after payment can create a signed negative balance (`credit_due`), shown separately as a carrier credit balance. Record an actual external refund using bank direction `carrier_refund`; cash debits and carrier payable credits settle that balance. Reversing an adjustment or refund appends its opposite and preserves prior approvals/bank history. Additional signed 210s remain unposted in finance classification until a named decision.

## Bank reconciliation

**Carrier credit applications** in this workspace record actual carrier-confirmed allocations from an existing credit-bearing settlement to 1–100 other prepared invoices for that carrier. They post carrier payable between loads, preserve invoice costs and bank history, and require current balances/versions plus named confirmation. Reversal/correction retains original proof and can reopen already-paid targets. Application files and every affected load's supporting evidence are checked transactionally. Current positive payables and negative credits stay separately visible until an actual recorded allocation/refund/payment resolves them. [Complete workflow and limits](carrier-credit-applications.md).

Record the actual external account label, bank reference, cleared date, bank amount, and reconciliation note. Allocate the amount to 1–100 customer invoices or prepared settlements. Every allocation is positive and uses the target's current version. Its total must equal the cleared bank amount exactly. A batch belongs to one customer for receipts/customer refunds or one carrier for payouts/carrier refunds. Customer refunds require actual confirmation and can consume only existing refund liabilities, including those on void cancellation invoices. Overpayments, stale allocations, duplicate targets, future clearing dates, and mixed counterparties are rejected atomically.

An account label plus bank reference can have only one active reconciliation, across all four directions. Idempotency replay returns the original result and does not post again. Distinct concurrent keys cannot bypass the bank-reference or outstanding-balance guards.

To correct an entry, reverse it with a reason and date. Reversal appends the opposite journal and reopens its balances; it does not reverse a bank transfer. The original entry, allocations, actor, and posting remain. A corrected record must explicitly identify the uncorrected reversed entry in `corrects_id` and keep that exact account, bank reference, and direction. It may correct amounts or allocation/counterparty mistakes. The old/new records link both ways; a correction chain cannot branch or reuse an active bank line. Each new batch must still have one counterparty and fit its current balances.

## Journals and integrity

| Action                               | Debit                           | Credit                         |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Customer invoice issuance            | Accounts receivable             | Freight revenue                |
| Customer credit                      | Freight revenue                 | Accounts receivable            |
| Carrier invoice approval             | Freight expense                 | Carrier payable                |
| Reconciled customer receipt          | Cash                            | Accounts receivable            |
| Reconciled customer refund           | Accounts receivable             | Cash                           |
| Reconciled carrier payout            | Carrier payable                 | Cash                           |
| Supplemental carrier debit           | Freight expense                 | Carrier payable                |
| Carrier credit/reducing revision     | Carrier payable                 | Freight expense                |
| Reconciled carrier refund            | Cash                            | Carrier payable                |
| Confirmed carrier credit application | Carrier payable on target loads | Carrier payable on source load |
| Reversal                             | Original credits                | Original debits                |

Every posting is balanced, positive on exactly one side per line, tied to its source record, and attributed to the authenticated subject. Multi-load bank entries retain each line's load ID. Reversals reference the original journal ID. Business state, journal, audit, and idempotency receipts commit together under the tenant row lock. A failed mutation retains none of its candidate postings.

The Journal workspace summarizes debit, credit, and net debit amounts by account. Cash is movement recorded by Freight, not the organization's complete bank balance. CSV exports preserve source/reversal/load IDs and escape spreadsheet formulas in text. Customer and carrier obligations shown outside the journal derive from the same active allocations. Back up the full workspace aggregate and document table together.

Qualification includes a known scenario: customer invoice 149,000 cents, credit 9,000, receipts 140,000, carrier cost/payout 118,000. The subledger closes with zero receivable/payable and 22,000 cents of cash movement. Reversals reopen the original balances without modifying old journal lines. PostgreSQL tests use independent instances and reconnect to verify concurrency, persistence, and absence of failed-request residue.

## Existing StateSet stack and limits

The implementation follows the exact-money, invoice-state, payment-idempotency, and reversing-journal patterns in `stateset-icommerce` revision `767f23f3b32d10c8744c8e4642d875382c811f40`, inspected in its invoice models, PostgreSQL invoice repository, and embedded general-ledger code. It stays inside Freight's PostgreSQL transaction rather than creating a second commerce database with an uncoordinated write.

This is the freight operational subledger. Bank feeds/payment execution, external GL posting, invoice delivery, tax determination, currency conversion/FX revaluation, accounting periods, revenue-recognition policy, customer prepayments/overpayments/credit applications, and regulatory invoice qualification are additional integrations/policies. Each shipment carries one currency (USD by default); its invoices, bills, cash, credits and journal postings stay in that currency and summaries are grouped per currency without conversion. See [multi-currency](multi-currency.md). The included inclusive invoice reflects your agreed freight amount; it does not calculate jurisdiction-specific tax. Do not treat a local posting or export as confirmation of a remote accounting/payment action.

Charge approvals preserve the base agreement and freeze with the relevant side's posted billing. Actual post-approval carrier changes use the separate adjustment workflow; later customer additions use separate supplemental customer invoices. Cancelled shipments use [independent cancellation-fee obligations](cancellations.md) with explicit finance decisions, invoices/payables, retained paid-fee reversals/refunds, and the existing bank/credit-application ledger. Their original transport rates do not post. Consolidated multi-load invoice allocation and automatic accessorial pricing remain further work. Recorded gate duration does not establish a payable or customer charge.

Freight billing is separate from commerce product-order totals. The sync integration continues to write shipment tracking only; it does not overwrite an upstream order's sales, payment, or accounting state.

# Native iCommerce bridge

Freight uses the engine's `stateset-primitives` typed IDs, `CurrencyCode` and `Money` through `stateset-freight-commerce`, plus `stateset-pricing` for its currency scale lookup and reporting-only rounding. Freight does not use the pricing crate's tax, promotion, line-item or order-total calculations. Both crates are pinned at 1.39.0. The exact upstream source, commit, hashes and MIT/Apache notices are retained in `vendor/stateset-primitives/UPSTREAM.json` and `vendor/stateset-pricing/UPSTREAM.json`. Their standalone manifests resolve workspace metadata; library source is unchanged. `web/tests/money.test.mjs` fails if the browser's copied currency scale table in `web/lib/money.mjs` differs from the vendored `currency_decimal_places`. This build does not depend on a sibling checkout or an unverified registry publication. The broader embedded commerce engine and its database do not run inside Freight.

Freight owns transportation plans, carrier tenders, buy/sell rates, stops, custody, documents, billing and recovery. iCommerce owns merchandise orders, fulfillment, inventory, packing, labels and native shipment records. Order merchandise totals never become freight prices. Money uses exact decimal strings and integer minor units at each currency's scale, including signed 64-bit boundaries; excess precision and overflow fail rather than round, and no workflow converts currency. Native HTTP DTOs do not provide the complete physical freight plan: operators supply its customer, route, equipment, weight and rates explicitly.

## Configure a tenant

Set an entry in operator-owned `FREIGHT_INTEGRATIONS_JSON`:

```json
{"acme":{"commerce_url":"https://commerce.example.com","commerce_token":"replace-with-a-tenant-authorized-token-at-least-32-characters","commerce_tenant_id":"acme"}}
```

The upstream HTTP deployment must enable tenant routing and authorize that credential for the configured tenant. Requests send `Authorization: Bearer …` and `x-tenant-id`; the freight workspace and native tenant are independent namespaces. Native origins require HTTPS, with HTTP allowed only on loopback for local development. Origins cannot contain paths, queries or credentials; redirects are refused and responses are bounded to 2 MiB. Native and legacy Sync order sources are mutually exclusive per freight tenant. EDI may coexist. Do not change providers for existing imported loads: their retained provider identity prevents silent retargeting. Reconfiguring a connection does not retarget already queued native handoffs.

## Import

Operations staff can list `/v1/commerce/orders?page=1`, inspect `/v1/commerce/orders/{id}`, then POST `/v1/commerce/import` with an `Idempotency-Key`:

```json
{"order_id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","load":{"reference":"CUSTOMER-LOAD-1","customer_id":"existing-freight-customer","mode":"FTL","equipment":"Dry van","commodity":"Goods","weight_lbs":1000,"miles":173,"origin":{"facility":"Origin","city":"Portland","state":"OR","date":"2026-10-23","address_lines":["15 Dock Street"],"postal_code":"97201","country":"US"},"destination":{"facility":"Destination","city":"Seattle","state":"WA","date":"2026-10-24","address_lines":["25 Receiving Avenue"],"postal_code":"98101","country":"US"},"buy_cents":123456,"sell_cents":150000}}
```

Use real dates/addresses and reviewed rates. The API fetches source identity and quantities itself; callers cannot inject source snapshots or upstream credentials. Only pending/confirmed/processing, unfulfilled orders with no shipped units qualify as new forward loads. Cancelled, held, unknown and partially/completely fulfilled orders are retained for source review but refused as new imports. Existing `/v1/sync/orders` and `/v1/sync/import` also use the tenant's configured provider, preserving the dashboard import flow. Original imports replay from the Freight receipt even when the source has changed or become unavailable.

The existing source observation and explicit review rules protect imported loads. Later changes in merchandise quantities, fulfillment or status can hold new commitments; physical custody/history remain intact. No native import emits legacy Sync tracking writeback.

## Review one shipment step

Complete warehouse packing and carrier handoff in iCommerce. The native shipment must belong to the original order and its product/SKU manifest must exactly cover all imported quantities. Partial shipments require a separate allocation workflow and cannot be advanced as if they represented the entire load.

The dashboard exposes this review on imported native loads, using the existing encrypted original-save journal. The iCommerce integration card opens native order import. API/MCP clients can use the same protected operations.

Once Freight is physically `in_transit` or `delivered`:

1. GET `/v1/loads/{load_id}/commerce-tracking?shipment_id={native_shipment_uuid}`. Inspect the native manifest, current status/version, load version and proposed next step.
2. POST the same route with a fresh `Idempotency-Key` and `{expected_load_version, shipment_id, expected_shipment_version}` from that review. The server verifies the native record again, refreshes the source and atomically queues the frozen handoff with its audit and receipt. Another unresolved native handoff for that load blocks new intent. The first queued handoff also binds the load to that native shipment UUID permanently through retained history; completing it does not permit a different native shipment to reuse the same physical delivery.
3. Inspect the integration queue. `synced` records the exact version/status confirmation or an explicitly described observed convergence. For a delivered load, repeat a new preview/review after each confirmed step until native delivery is complete.

The legal forward steps are `shipped`/`failed` → `in_transit` → `out_for_delivery` → `delivered`. One review queues one step. Freight does not jump from shipped to delivered, reverse an advanced native state, or create/pack/allocate a native shipment. PATCH bodies contain only `expected_version` and `status`. Tracking numbers, carrier labels, addresses, prices and inventory are never fabricated or overwritten by this bridge.

## Find native shipments

Operations can browse `GET /v1/loads/{id}/commerce-shipments?page=1` from the load detail's **Find order shipments** picker. Freight derives the order UUID from the retained native import and fixes the upstream origin, credential and tenant from operator configuration. Only one positive bounded `page` is accepted; caller-supplied order, tenant, URL, offset and filter overrides are refused. Each native request fixes `order_id`, `limit=25` and the checked page offset. The upstream page must match those bounds and contain unique same-order shipment identities; an invalid or unrelated row refuses the entire response. The adapter keeps its 2 MiB response bound and never exposes upstream recipient/address/price fields through this list.

Rows include native shipment number, identity, status and version, plus `ready_for_review`, `blocked` or `up_to_date` and an explanation. Partial manifests, warehouse-only states and a different retained shipment UUID cannot start another step. Existing pending/sending/retry/held native jobs are shown and block a second handoff. The list is read-only: it creates no local receipt, job or source observation and sends no native PATCH. Source holds remain in force at confirmation.

Selection returns only a shipment identity and fetches the existing individual tracking preview afresh. It does not use the discovery page as a write body. Confirmation then re-fetches the native record, checks the reviewed versions and verifies canonical source readiness as before. Changes observed in the current load version, verified owner or native handoff invalidate the dashboard list and preview. Manual UUID entry remains available. Pages reflect live records rather than a stable snapshot; native total counts are informational, and `has_more` comes from the upstream bounded overfetch contract.

## Uncertain outcomes

Native shipment PATCH has optimistic version checks but no durable idempotency receipt. Freight freezes the original version/body, native identity, manifest, origin and tenant in its outbox. A failed/invalid/interrupted response or expired sending lease moves the job to `held`; automatic retry stops. The original Freight request can replay its local queue receipt without another upstream fetch or queue insertion. The save-resolution endpoint can recover or fence an uncertain local enqueue using the original route, body and key.

Inspect the held job and native shipment before explicitly POSTing `/v1/outbox/{id}/retry` with a new local retry key. The dispatcher first reads the native record. Exact original next-version/status/manifest convergence completes the job with a message that the original PATCH receipt is unavailable; it does not claim proof of which writer committed it. If the original version/status/manifest remain unchanged, the explicit retry sends that original PATCH. Any other version, manifest, order identity or connection binding keeps the job held. It never rebases onto a newer native version or automatically queues a different lifecycle step. Source holds also continue to apply. Retain and investigate unresolved jobs instead of deleting their history.

## Review externally advanced handoffs

When another native writer has moved a held shipment beyond its original expected version, Operations can preview `GET /v1/outbox/{id}/commerce-review`. The native record must retain the complete original manifest and order identity, the original fixed origin/tenant binding, and a strictly greater version. An unchanged version stays held because its original PATCH could still apply. Active leases, altered manifests and changed connections refuse review.

After investigating external activity, POST that path with `expected_load_version`, `expected_total_attempts`, `expected_shipment_version`, and genuine `contact`, `reference`, and `note` (each 1–200 bytes without control characters). The server fetches the native record again and checks current local versions under the tenant transaction. The observed greater native version fences a late original optimistic write; it does not establish which writer applied the original PATCH. The resulting `external_reviewed` status retires only the old local handoff. It retains the original payload, identity, transmission and attempt history, records the actor and observation, and keeps `original_patch_outcome: "unknown"`. It changes neither native shipment nor physical Freight status and sends no PATCH.

The staff Integration handoffs queue exposes this review and its recorded evidence. Its confirmation uses the encrypted original-save journal. Replay with the exact original key/body returns the original local receipt without native access; the original-save resolver can recover a completed review or fence an uncommitted one. Integration-only and viewer roles cannot perform this operations decision. A source hold does not prevent retiring old intent; fresh source checks still gate any new commitment. A next lifecycle step requires a separate fresh shipment preview and confirmation. The retained native shipment UUID binding survives retirement.

## Persistence and qualification

Native snapshots, plans and connection bindings use existing generic source/outbox/receipt fields; no secret is persisted in a handoff. Migration 029 extends the existing order-source wakeup projection to native jobs, recomputing changed scheduling deadlines without rewriting original queue bodies, workspace timestamps or history revisions. The canonical storage format is unchanged. Older workers do not recognize the native destination and their configuration parser rejects native connection fields; deploy the current API and workers together rather than mixing binaries during activation.

# Reviewed native movement times

Operations can correct an applied native carrier pickup or delivery **actual time** from shipment details. The original authenticated carrier report remains unchanged. A correction appends evidence; it does not retract custody, rewind shipment status, change location or the latest tracking timestamp, revise a carrier agreement, accept POD, or move money.

## Review the original report

Open **Native movement time review**, inspect the original actual time, carrier reference, and authenticated reporting actor, then choose **Correct pickup time** or **Correct delivery time**. Enter the corrected UTC instant, actual carrier contact, supporting reference, and findings. Confirm that the exact original report and supporting evidence were reviewed. Previous corrections remain visible with their original actor and recording time.

The named operations actor attests to this review. The correction does not claim that the original carrier user authenticated or approved the new time. External driver/facility correspondence remains operator-attested evidence. A raw database owner could rewrite records and hashes; these digests detect retained-evidence corruption under the application's write contract, not a malicious database administrator.

Only an applied native `pickup` or `delivery` report belonging to the current load, tender, and carrier can be corrected, while the load is in transit or delivered. Location reports, `stale_ignored` reports, retired assignments, raw EDI documents, physical status changes, and movement retractions are outside this workflow. EDI processing timestamps remain distinct from actual stop times. Correct source evidence rather than changing a correct gate/service time to force agreement.

## Atomic source-bound correction

`POST /v1/carrier-submissions/{id}/time-corrections` requires `operations.write`, an idempotency key, and exactly these fields:

```json
{
  "expected_load_version": 12,
  "source_sha256": "<the exact source digest from movement_sources>",
  "expected_previous_id": null,
  "observed_at": "2026-10-15T17:30:00Z",
  "contact": "Actual carrier dispatch supervisor",
  "reference": "Actual driver and facility correction reference",
  "note": "Reviewed findings supporting this corrected actual time"
}
```

Use the latest correction ID as `expected_previous_id` for a later correction. The endpoint rejects unknown fields, future or unchanged times, missing findings, changed source bytes, a stale load version, and a changed correction predecessor. Actor and recording time are server-owned. A successful retry returns its original receipt even after later corrections; a failed request consumes no key.

The source digest binds the entire canonically serialized stored carrier submission, including its original time, actor, offer/tender/carrier identity, reference, note, location, and outcome; it is not a digest of the original HTTP request bytes. Each correction retains that digest and a digest of its own evidence, plus an explicit predecessor. Verification checks every retained link and the original source, including superseded corrections. A corrupt source, correction, or chain exposes an evidence-review hold rather than silently accepting a different time. Restore/reconcile original records through controlled incident recovery; this endpoint cannot approve corrupt history.

The existing tenant transaction commits the correction, incremented load version, named audit, idempotency receipt, and fresh Sync snapshot together. Competing reviews against one version cannot both commit. The immutable rate document and its original SHA-256 remain unchanged. The financial evidence lock includes an approved carrier invoice, any prepared settlement, or any nonvoid customer bill, including a draft. Correct actual times before those commitments; this workflow does not rewrite posted finance.

## Timeline, privacy, and integration

The [shared chronology](execution-timeline.md) uses the effective corrected time. It still validates all known route-ordered arrival/service/departure facts. A correction cannot introduce a contradiction or leave its own source contradictory. Independent older conflicts can be repaired incrementally; finance and final delivery writeback remain held until the complete required evidence is consistent. Intermediate service boundaries use corrected native pickup/delivery times rather than the original mistaken timestamp.

Staff receive the exact original source and retained correction history. Carrier/customer timelines show the effective time, a correction marker, and the original time without staff contact, reference, findings, or actor. The original carrier's own submission history retains its original time and additionally identifies its effective corrected time. Retired offer scope remains historical.

Sync receives `trackingData.freight_actual_milestones`, an array containing only `kind`, effective `observed_at`, and `corrected`. New native reports are included in the snapshot created by their own transaction. Correction snapshots retain the same source order UUID, physical status/location, route, and tracking watermark. No private correction evidence enters this metadata. These custom fields survive in Sync's raw tracking JSON; its typed canonical order projection does not expose arbitrary Freight metadata. Existing queued payloads and completed writebacks remain immutable, ordered, and subject to the existing source/route/chronology holds. An invalid current correction chain also holds final delivery updates.

No EDI source document is rewritten or sent as a replacement movement by this operation. Existing signed callbacks, native reports, and rate-confirmation transport keep their original contracts.

## Persistence and qualification

Migration `018_movement_corrections.sql` advances storage format 15 to **16**, fencing older writers/workers that could discard corrections or ignore effective chronology. It verifies prior markers and changes only format markers, preserving original business fields, timestamps, documents, and migration history. Missing older `movement_corrections` defaults to an empty collection when decoded. See [deployment and rollback](storage.md).

# Multi-currency shipments

Each shipment has one ISO-style currency, set when it is created (`currency` on `POST /v1/loads`, a quote plan or a carrier contract rate). It defaults to USD. Every financial record that hangs off the shipment uses that same currency and never converts it: carrier invoices and documents, charges, rate confirmations, cancellation fees, customer bills and supplements, cash entries, credits, carrier credit applications and journal postings.

## Rules

- **Codes and scale.** Any three-letter code is accepted and normalized to upper case. Amounts are integer minor units at the currency's scale from `vendor/stateset-primitives` (`currency_decimal_places`): 2 decimals by default, 0 for JPY/KRW/CLP and similar, 3 for BHD/KWD/OMR and similar, 8 for BTC/ETH. Every amount is limited to 0–100,000,000 minor units. Rounding is never applied.
- **Matching.** A carrier invoice, cash entry or credit whose currency differs from its shipment or bill is refused. Carrier credits only transfer between settlements in the same currency. A contract rate is only a candidate for a quote in the same currency.
- **Amendments.** A customer amendment re-prices the booked shipment in place, so it must keep the shipment's currency. A different currency is a new agreement.
- **Imports.** `POST /v1/sync/import` and `/v1/commerce/import` use the source order's `currency` when the load plan omits one. Freight can be priced in a different currency from the goods, so an explicit plan currency always wins. A missing or malformed order code falls back to USD. The web import form prefills the order's currency.
- **Plan revisions.** `POST /v1/loads/{id}/plan` keeps the load's existing currency when the revised plan omits `currency`. An explicit currency on a planned, uninvoiced load is still honored.
- **Summaries.** `finance.currencies` lists one group per currency. The legacy top-level totals (`receivable_cents`, `overdue_cents`, and so on) are the USD group only, and are zero when a tenant has no USD activity. Nothing is summed across currencies.
- **Compatibility.** Stored USD records serialize without a `currency` field (quote plans, contract rates, catalog settlement rows), so their bytes and digests are unchanged. A missing currency always means USD.

## Interfaces

- **Web.** All amounts are formatted through `web/lib/money.mjs`, which mirrors the server's scale table exactly (browser CLDR data differs for some codes). USD shows as `$1,500.00`. Other currencies keep their code visible, for example `EUR €1,500.00` or `CAD $10.00`, so a dollar sign never stands for a non-USD amount. Load, quote and contract forms take a currency. Quotes from a source shipment and amendments lock it. The cash form picks a bank currency and only lists targets in that currency. Dashboard and finance totals are shown per currency, and margin percentages only appear when a single currency is in view.
- **Terminal.** Billing and Payables rows show USD amounts unchanged and prefix other amounts with their code (`EUR 1500.00`). The summary strip keeps its "USD" labels for USD-only tenants. Otherwise it lists each non-zero currency separately (`1500.00 · EUR 100.00`).
- **CSV.** The load-board export adds a final `Currency` column; see [load exports](load-exports.md).

## Not included

There is no FX conversion, revaluation, multi-currency settlement of one invoice, or currency-specific tax. `stateset_freight_commerce::convert_money` exists for reporting with caller-supplied rates; it is not used in posting.

# Multi-stop freight execution

Create or revise an ordered route with origin pickup, up to eighteen intermediate pickups/deliveries, and final delivery. Each intermediate stop has a stable `stop_` identifier, service kind, facility, street/postal address, planned date, contact, and instructions. The editor supports adding, removing, and reordering stops. Dates must follow route order. Tendering and quoting require complete addresses; drafts can retain incomplete addresses for later correction.

The route is part of the exact customer quote, carrier rate confirmation, release document, and customer billing snapshot. Revisions preserve the original documents and hashes. A two-endpoint lane contract cannot price intermediate stops: obtain an explicit carrier offer covering the entire route. A previously confirmed appointment prevents changing its stop details or route position until actual cancellation is recorded.

## Carrier agreement and EDI boundary

The current sibling EDI `Tender204` model represents origin and destination only. It ignores unknown intermediate-stop metadata and its builder emits no S5 route stops. Freight therefore retains these tenders as `native_only`, with zero transmission attempts. Operator retry and worker selection independently prevent a partial 204 handoff, including a job whose persisted queue status is incorrectly changed to pending. Ordinary two-stop 204s continue through the existing adapter.

Issue and explicitly publish the full carrier rate confirmation. The assigned carrier reviews the exact document/hash and accepts through the authenticated portal. An unsolicited 990 cannot establish initial acceptance of the missing full route. Publication establishes a real communication channel, so the tender cannot subsequently be withdrawn as proven unsent. Use the existing carrier release workflow if necessary. Retired offers retain their original route/document without exposing a replacement carrier's plan or execution.

## Actual intermediate service

After physical origin pickup, operations or the currently assigned authenticated carrier confirms each intermediate stop in order. Record the actual UTC service time, facility contact, evidence reference, and findings. Arrival alone does not establish unloading or additional pickup. Missing earlier service cannot be silently filled by confirming a later stop.

Each record binds the exact stop snapshot, current tender, authenticated actor, original recording time, and evidence digest. Carrier submissions additionally bind the carrier's publication. Replaying a successful request returns the original record. Stale versions, duplicates, wrong carriers, and out-of-order observations fail atomically. Operations can explicitly correct a record; corrections append a successor and retain every original. The entire correction chain must remain intact before service is treated as complete. Approved carrier invoices, prepared settlements, and nonvoid customer invoice drafts/issued invoices lock further service changes.

Every stop supports facility-confirmed appointment windows and actual gate observations. Window starts must follow route order in UTC. Known gate times follow the full route, and intermediate service must fall between known arrival and departure. Departure requires actual service confirmation. Corrections revalidate the known sequence and retain the original appointment baseline and facility snapshot. Unobserved arrivals/departures remain unknown. See [appointments and gates](stops.md).

The [shared execution timeline](execution-timeline.md) additionally enforces chronology across gates, intermediate service, and native origin/final movement. It supports explicit repair of older conflicts and holds finance/final Sync until all known times agree.

## Delivery, finance, and Sync

Native carrier reporting and the operations delivery command require every intermediate confirmation. A signed final EDI D1 remains physical evidence of final delivery even if intermediate confirmations are missing. Freight preserves that observation, displays a route attention item, and continues holding finance and final Sync delivery writeback. This supports late entry of actual intermediate evidence without erasing the original delivery fact.

All intermediate services and finance-reviewed consolidated POD are required for carrier invoice approval, settlement, and customer billing. Service confirmations do not create charges, approve invoices, or execute payments. Consolidated POD must be reviewed against the entire route; per-line item quantities, partial loss allocation, and a separate signed POD for every stop are not implemented.

For imported orders, the existing ordered Sync queue retains the original order UUID. Tracking includes minimal ordered route identity, stop kind/location/date, service completion, and `freight_route_complete`. Private contacts, findings, actors, and evidence references stay in Freight. An incomplete final-delivery payload becomes `local_only`; a later complete-route payload can proceed. Actual Sync canonical reads retain supported camelCase fields, while arbitrary route metadata remains in its raw tracking JSON.

## API and persistence

- Load/quote plans accept optional `intermediate_stops: [{id, kind: "pickup"|"delivery", stop: {...}}]`; `stop` uses the existing stop shape. Empty arrays are omitted from persisted commercial snapshots to preserve legacy document bases.
- `POST /v1/loads/{id}/stop-services` requires `operations.write`.
- `POST /v1/stop-services/{id}/correct` requires `operations.write` and targets the current original/successor.
- `POST /v1/portal/offers/{id}/stop-services` requires `portal.carrier.report`, current carrier ownership, and current publication.
- Each request requires an `Idempotency-Key` and `{expected_load_version, stop_id, observed_at, contact, reference, note}`. The server derives the assignment, actor, recording time, and digest. Contact/reference/findings require 1–200 characters.
- Workspace responses include immutable `stop_services`, per-load `itinerary`, and `route_attention`. Carrier projections expose only current route completion/times plus that carrier's own submitted history.

Multi-stop plans were introduced by storage format 14 and migration 016. Format 15 adds shared execution chronology and final-tracking holds; format 16 adds retained native movement corrections and effective-time validation/writeback. Current format 17 adds source-derived operations work with retained ownership/follow-up history. These migrations preserve existing business fields, files, timestamps, and checksummed migration history. PostgreSQL tenant locking commits service evidence, load version, audit, receipt, and Sync enqueue together. See [storage deployment](storage.md).
