# Staff SSO with the existing StateSet Clerk instance

Shared-workspace browser recovery also needs a server-only `FREIGHT_SAVE_JOURNAL_KEYS_JSON` keyring or a valid `FREIGHT_SESSION_SECRET`. Configure it on every web replica and retain old encryption keys for unresolved originals. See [encrypted recovery and key rotation](sealed-save-journal.md). These keys are separate from Clerk’s public publishable key and must never be browser variables.

Freight supports staff sign-in through Clerk, matching the identity provider used in `stateset-app` (`lib/clerk-context.js`, `lib/server-security.js`, and its Clerk 5.61.9 React dependency were inspected). Freight uses standard v2 Clerk session tokens, not StateSet App's Hasura JWT template or browser organization metadata. The Rust API makes the tenant/role decision for every request.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[Clerk sign-in and organization selection] --> S[React SDK: short-lived session JWT]
  S --> W[Next.js gateway: fixed organization context]
  W --> A[Rust API: signature, issuer, origin, expiry]
  A --> P[Clerk: live session and organization membership]
  P --> G[Deployment-owned organization and role mapping]
  G --> T[Existing Freight tenant and capabilities]
```

Counterparty-scoped carrier/customer organizations use the same signed-session/live-membership checks, with explicit server-owned `counterparty_id` and partner-only roles. See [partner configuration and `/portal`](partner-portal.md). Staff organizations remain unscoped and cannot mix with partner grants.

## Configure a real staff workspace

1. Use the Clerk instance already used by StateSet App. Enable/confirm your organization's SSO, staff enrollment, MFA policy, and allowed Freight application domain/redirects in that instance. No Clerk account, organization, invitation, or domain was created by this implementation.
2. Set `FREIGHT_DEMO=false` on both real services and configure PostgreSQL. On the Rust API, set `FREIGHT_CLERK_JSON` using the **actual immutable Clerk organization IDs**, existing canonical Freight tenant IDs, and explicit Clerk-role-to-Freight-role mappings:

```dotenv
FREIGHT_CLERK_JSON='{"issuer":"https://clerk.stateset.com","secret_key":"replace-with-your-real-Clerk-backend-secret","authorized_parties":["https://freight.your-domain.example"],"organizations":{"org_your_actual_id":{"tenant_id":"your_existing_freight_tenant","roles":{"org:freight_viewer":"viewer","org:freight_operations":"operations","org:freight_finance":"finance","org:freight_admin":"admin"}}}}'
```

The issuer is the configured Clerk Frontend API origin; use your actual instance rather than copying an example blindly. The backend secret is server-only. Do not put it in browser variables, source files, URLs, or public organization metadata. An organization cannot choose its own Freight tenant through its name, slug, endpoint metadata, or request headers. Unlisted organizations and unmapped roles receive 403. Clerk's built-in `org:admin` has **no implicit Freight administrator grant**; map roles deliberately. Membership may change dynamically in Clerk without issuing staff API credentials or restarting Freight.

3. On the Next.js web service, set:

```dotenv
FREIGHT_WEB_AUTH_MODE=clerk
FREIGHT_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_live_replace_with_your_public_key
FREIGHT_WEB_ORIGIN=https://freight.your-domain.example
FREIGHT_API_URL=http://your-private-freight-api:8090
```

The public key must belong to the same Clerk instance. These values are read at runtime; the public key is the only Clerk configuration returned in page props. `FREIGHT_WEB_ORIGIN` is fixed for mutation-origin validation. HTTPS is required outside loopback development. In this mode, the credential login endpoint and old encrypted workspace cookies cannot grant browser access. Staff must select an active approved organization; personal accounts cannot open a tenant. The organization switcher and account controls stay available when a selected organization has no Freight grant. Provider load failure shows an explicit retry screen with no credential fallback. SDK telemetry is disabled.

4. Keep `FREIGHT_API_KEYS_JSON` for explicitly authorized machine/EDI/sync access, or set it to `{}` for an SSO-only API. Static credentials retain their existing tenant/subject/role behavior. The API can run with Clerk and no static keys. Signed EDI callbacks and integration workers retain their existing independent credentials and are not made dependent on a browser staff session.
5. Configure the same instance/org/tenant/role mappings consistently across API replicas. Restart replicas after changing deployment mappings. `compose.yaml` forwards the secret JSON only to the API and the publishable key/mode only to the web service.

## Request verification and revocation

- Only RS256 signed v2 session tokens from the configured issuer/JWKS are accepted. Authorized-party (`azp`) origins must match exactly. `sub`, `sid`, `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`, version, and selected organization are required/checked; token lifetime is at most 120 seconds. Expired, future, pending, impersonated, wrong-origin, wrong-issuer, wrong-algorithm, or unscoped tokens cannot grant access. Header key URLs and browser role/tenant claims are not authorization inputs.
- The API checks the live Clerk session's user/status/expiry and the user's current organization membership on **every request**, including reads and idempotency replay. It verifies the returned user/organization and maps the live membership role through server configuration. Those grants are not cached. Revocation, removal, or role downgrade affects subsequent requests using the same still-signed token. A provider error/rate limit/malformed response fails closed with a generic 503 rather than accepting a stale grant. Already authenticated in-flight requests are not retroactively canceled by a later membership change.
- JWKS public keys are cached for up to five minutes. An unknown key ID refreshes the cache with a one-second retry throttle; rotation is tested against a real signed-token fixture. HTTP redirects are disabled and response sizes/timeouts are bounded. Backend secrets go only to Clerk's fixed `https://api.clerk.com/v1` endpoints. Local issuer/BAPI overrides are restricted to explicit API demo mode and HTTP loopback fixtures.
- An optional `audience` in `FREIGHT_CLERK_JSON` requires that exact audience on the default session token. With no configured audience, tokens carrying a separate audience are rejected. Configure default session claims accordingly; the frontend does not request a Hasura/custom JWT template.
- Clerk's React SDK obtains fresh session tokens. Requests retain the organization that rendered their form; the gateway forwards an explicit organization guard and the API compares it against verified identity. Organization changes remount the workspace. A stale operation cannot silently post into the newly selected tenant. Downloads use the short-lived `__session` cookie plus the same organization guard in the URL; **no token is put in URLs**. Known IDs from another tenant still return 404.
- The audit subject is `clerk:<immutable user ID>`, never a submitted username or browser role. Existing business rules, document integrity, expected versions, transaction locks, and finance approvals still apply. Logout uses Clerk's session sign-out/revocation flow; the old static-credential browser cookie cannot act as fallback in SSO mode.

Clerk's short-lived `__session` cookie follows its SDK/session design; it is not Freight's encrypted eight-hour `HttpOnly` credential cookie. Credential mode remains available for the existing local/demo workflow and explicit credentials. See Clerk's primary [session token](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/sessions/session-tokens), [manual verification](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/sessions/manual-jwt-verification), [session lookup](https://clerk.com/docs/reference/backend/sessions/get-session), and [cookie/session design](https://clerk.com/docs/guides/how-clerk-works/overview) documentation.

## Qualification and commissioning

Local tests generate/sign real RSA JWTs against an owned issuer/JWKS/session/membership fixture. They verify live role changes before replay, user/session binding, tenant isolation, pending/impersonated/expired/future/wrong-origin/forged tokens, required audience, signing-key rotation, provider outages, configuration validation, and stable audit identity. Browser tests run a second standalone web service in Clerk mode and exercise authenticated reads/writes, exact document bytes, downloads, removed membership, revocation, stale-organization submission, and rejection of old credential cookies. The SDK failure screen is exercised with external identity traffic blocked. Test private keys are intentionally public fixture material and are not production credentials.

The actual external Clerk sign-in, enterprise SSO/MFA redirect, real organization's role assignments, production domain registration, logout, and membership revocation must be commissioned with your own instance and authorized staff. No live provider credential or staff account was used locally. Verify two real organizations with an overlapping user, role downgrade, membership removal, session logout/replay, and cross-tenant document IDs before enabling production staff access. A working synthetic fixture is not evidence of a configured live instance.

This provides tenant-wide **staff** access. Customer/carrier portal filtering, independent invoice-entry/approval duties, and your provider's invitation/SCIM policies require their own configuration/workflows. Freight does not automatically create or invite users or edit organization grants in Clerk.

# Stop addresses, appointments, and gate evidence

Origin, intermediate pickups/deliveries, and final delivery share these appointment and gate controls. Ordered routes support up to twenty stops. See [multi-stop planning and actual service](multi-stop.md) for full-route documents, native carrier acceptance, service evidence, and financial/Sync holds.

Load plans now contain street addresses, postal/country codes, contacts, phone numbers, and instructions for pickup and delivery. The browser requires street/postal details when creating or revising a plan. API drafts and legacy records may omit them, but each new tender requires both stops to have one or two nonempty street lines and a postal code. Missing data is never filled with a guessed real address. Synthetic demo stops use explicitly synthetic addresses.

The `stateset-edi` 204 receives the actual stop addresses through its supported `Party` fields and emits N3/N4 segments. Wire fields enforce ASCII and length/delimiter limits: facility 60, city 30, each street line 55, at most two lines, postal code 15, and uppercase two-letter state/country codes. This is the current gateway-compatible address format, not worldwide postal validation or geocoding. Contact/phone/instructions remain operating information in Freight; the gateway request model has no appointment-window or stop-instruction field. Share windows and instructions directly with the carrier.

## Facility-confirmed appointment windows

In load details, select **Book pickup appointment** or **Book delivery appointment**. Enter facility-local start/end times, the IANA timezone, the actual facility contact, external confirmation reference, and note. Booking records human-confirmed coordination; it does not reserve capacity in a facility system or send a carrier message. Coordinate changes with the facility and carrier before recording them.

The start's local date must match the planned stop date, the end must be at/after the start within 48 hours, and all active appointment starts must follow full route order in UTC. Overnight windows are supported. Time resolution uses the supplied timezone's rules, rather than the browser/server timezone. A spring-forward time that does not exist is rejected. A fall-back time that occurs twice requires an explicit earlier/later choice; the default asks for clarification. Records retain the supplied local times, timezone/choice, resolved UTC instants, creator, and proof.

Carrier insurance and an assigned driver's license must cover the final local day of every active window. Tender/dispatch use that extended date as well as the planned delivery date and today. Booking/rescheduling an assigned shipment cannot extend beyond the recorded qualifications; record actual renewed qualifications before extending the appointment.

Rescheduling supersedes the old appointment and links the replacement; cancellation records its actor/reason. Both preserve prior windows and confirmation evidence. After a current-assignment gate arrival, its appointment baseline cannot be rescheduled or cancelled to hide lateness. Completed stop appointments also remain. Cancel a booked appointment before revising its stop details/date in the load plan. Cancelling a load or releasing a carrier does not claim the facility cancelled its booking; record actual facility cancellation separately. An active booking is retained across re-tendering until explicitly replaced/cancelled.

The [shared execution timeline](execution-timeline.md) checks gates against actual service at every other stop and native origin/final movement. A correction preserves the original and must not introduce a contradiction. Independent historical conflicts can be repaired one at a time while finance stays held.

## Actual arrival and departure

**Record pickup/delivery arrival** records an observed gate time, timezone, evidence reference, and note against the current carrier attempt and the appointment in force. Actual times cannot be more than five minutes ahead of the server clock. Arrival requires an accepted carrier assignment; delivery arrival requires pickup evidence in the shipment lifecycle. Departure requires a recorded gate arrival and the corresponding pickup/delivery lifecycle milestone.

Gate times never advance shipment status, assign fleet equipment, invent a POD, or establish finance approval. A truck can arrive while loading/unloading remains pending. Record pickup/delivery through the existing commands or authenticated carrier evidence. The 214 codec's local clock/status observations are retained in their original audit evidence; they are not automatically reinterpreted as timezone-qualified gate times.

Known gate instants must follow pickup arrival/departure, each intermediate arrival/service/departure, then final delivery arrival/departure. Missing observations remain missing; recording delivery arrival does not fabricate an origin gate record. Duplicate records require **Correct pickup/delivery arrival/departure**. A correction appends a new record linked to its predecessor, requires supporting evidence and the current load version, and revalidates the whole known sequence. Original records remain readable. Current stop summaries and corrections are scoped to the active tender attempt; released-carrier gate evidence stays historical.

## Attention, timing, and financial meaning

Current stop cards show the confirmed window, early/on-time/late arrival, minutes after the window, and dwell. Known arrival/departure pairs yield elapsed whole minutes. While the stop remains open, an arrival without departure shows elapsed time since arrival. If the physical stop has completed but departure is missing, completed dwell remains unknown instead of accumulating a fictional dwell total. Missing arrivals after a booked window enter the overview/exception filter until arrival or physical completion resolves that attention condition. Metrics are computed when the workspace is read; they do not overwrite manually recorded shipment exceptions.

These measurements are operational evidence. They do not calculate detention eligibility, add a charge, alter buy/sell rates, create invoices, or post a journal. Contract free time, charge approval, and external billing agreements need their own verified financial workflow before automation.

## API, persistence, and sync-server

All stop mutations require operations permission, `Idempotency-Key`, and `expected_load_version`. Appointment/gate changes, load version, audit, receipt, and any sync handoff commit together under the tenant row lock. Concurrent booking against one version commits exactly one result. Existing PostgreSQL snapshots deserialize missing arrays/details safely.

- `POST /v1/loads/{id}/appointments` books/reschedules.
- `POST /v1/appointments/{id}/cancel` records facility cancellation.
- `POST /v1/loads/{id}/stop-events` records arrival/departure.
- `POST /v1/stop-events/{id}/correct` appends a correction.

Workspace responses include `appointments`, `stop_events`, and each load's `stop_execution` summary. See [request shapes](api.md).

For imported orders, appointment/gate mutations enqueue the existing ordered sync-server tracking endpoint. `trackingData.freight_stops` contains each stop's current window UTC instants/timezone and current-attempt `arrival_at`/`departure_at`. Evidence references, contact details, staff identities, and internal notes are excluded. Corrections update the original source order, and carrier release snapshots clear the old attempt's times. Subsequent appointment/gate/movement updates use the current assignment; retired carrier times do not leak into a replacement assignment. Sync-server currently stores arbitrary nonempty tracking JSON, so this uses its existing contract without changing that repository.

Verified evidence includes real-codec N3/N4 address compatibility, timezone/DST cases, booking history and baseline protection, atomic failure rollback, chronological corrections, missing-departure handling, retired-carrier isolation, actual HTTP sync writeback, PostgreSQL concurrent writers/reconnect, role denial, and a production browser workflow on desktop/mobile. Live dock-system booking, carrier communication, route optimization, and detention billing remain further work toward the full TMS.

# Carrier tender and release

Every offer is an independent tender attempt with a carrier snapshot, plan snapshot, authenticated creator, status, and carrier-facing shipment reference. Re-planning keeps the freight load ID/reference, source order UUID, BOL, and historical evidence. A replacement tender receives a new `SF-…` shipment reference even when the carrier is unchanged. Partners must echo the attempt's shipment reference in their 990, 214, and 210 documents.

## Withdraw an unsent offer

Use **Withdraw unsent tender** in load details to return an offer to planning. Local cancellation is also available for a planned load or a proven-unsent offer. No [partner portal publication](partner-portal.md) or non-retracted external [carrier rate-confirmation handoff](carrier-rate-confirmations.md) may exist for that tender, including prior document revisions. Every associated EDI job must still be `pending_handoff`, explicitly `not_started`, have zero current/cumulative attempts, and have no upstream response. Freight commits the withdrawal and supersedes only that attempt's jobs together.

An HTTP failure, timeout, expired lease, or reset retry cycle cannot establish that a carrier never received an offer. The dispatcher persists `transmission: attempted` before IO and retains cumulative attempts. Older rows without transmission evidence read as `unknown`; they cannot use local withdrawal. A portal publication, manually accepted assignment, or recorded external carrier rate-document handoff is a commitment even when its original HTTP handoff has not started. Issuing a rate document alone does not establish communication. A later report of an old/changed document being handed off creates a separate coordination hold; resolve that retained evidence with actual carrier findings before new commitments.

## Release a carrier before pickup

1. Open the load's tender history and select **Request carrier release**. Choose return to planning or cancel, and record a reason. Freight preserves the carrier assignment and pauses dispatch, new EDI attempts, and operator retries for that attempt.
2. Either publish the request through **Authenticated carrier release**, or contact the carrier through your actual operating channel. Establish whether it accepted the offer, has custody, and agrees to release the assignment. Publication makes the exact request available in the scoped carrier portal; it does not send an email or EDI cancellation.
3. The carrier can respond natively as described below. For genuine external correspondence, record the carrier contact, external confirmation reference, and substantive note. **Confirm carrier released** clears assignments and returns the load to planning or cancels it according to the request. **Confirm carrier retained** closes the request and resumes the existing assignment. External attestations record the authenticated operations subject and require the latest load version.
4. For re-planning, revise the plan and tender again. The old attempt, release proof, wire identity, and handoff history remain visible. Pickup/location and assignment changes continue to enqueue ordered sync-server tracking against the original source order.

Release can be requested while tendered, accepted, or dispatched, before pickup. A live HTTP handoff lease prevents release confirmation; allow it to finish or expire. Expired leases can be fenced without resending, even if the connection has since been disabled. Their previous transmission outcome remains uncertain. The old worker cannot update a replacement tender when its response arrives.

Existing carrier invoices or non-void customer invoices block release/re-tendering until their financial implications are reconciled; no invoice is silently reassigned or discarded. Current-carrier pickup evidence while a release is pending records the real movement and changes the request to `blocked_by_movement`. It creates an incident requiring investigation. Cancelling a load never substitutes for resolving physical custody.

## Staff confirmation context

The shared [shipment confirmation forms](shipment-confirmations.md) keep the shipment identity and version reviewed when opened. A background refresh cannot authorize an open tender or other action against a newly revised shipment. Changed shipments disable confirmation while retaining selections/notes; close the action and review the latest shipment before reopening it. An unseen competing update still receives the existing API version-conflict rejection.

## Authenticated carrier release

For a pending current pre-pickup request, operations publishes an explicit carrier message and a response/application deadline in UTC, no more than seven days ahead. The frozen document binds the exact tender shipment reference, carrier, lane, equipment, disposition, message, and deadline. Private operations reasons, customer identity, prices, and financial review details are excluded. Publishing or revising requires the reviewed load version and preceding publication ID; it retains the assignment and original documents. Open staff forms keep the identity/version that was reviewed even during background refresh.

The authenticated carrier sees **Carrier release requests** in `/portal`, with an exact document download. **Confirm carrier release** requires a contact, reference, substantive findings, the published document hash, current load version, and explicit confirmation that the carrier has not picked up and has no custody of this assignment. **Retain assignment** closes the request without inventing tender acceptance or physical movement. Release requires an unexpired deadline; retention remains available after expiry because it preserves ownership. Other carriers, customers, staff/service roles, superseded requests, replacement assignments, and pickup-blocked requests cannot submit that native response.

With no hold, the native response applies the existing release/retention rules atomically. A live handoff lease, financial evidence, or unresolved custody review retains a positive acknowledgement as `awaiting_operations`; the carrier assignment and pending request remain. This is not a successful shipment release. After resolving the hold, operations can **Apply recorded carrier release**. Application checks the current exact request/tender, latest publication, deadline, load version, custody, financial records, and leases again. It preserves the original carrier contact, actor, time, document hash, and evidence hash; the later operations actor/time are separate application evidence. Expired authorizations require a new publication and current carrier confirmation. A superseding publication cannot reuse the old response.

Actual pickup wins regardless of the order of competing transactions. A release that commits first leaves subsequent pickup as a retained former-carrier custody incident; pickup that commits first blocks the release. Expired HTTP leases are fenced by the existing release command, and a returning worker cannot overwrite the new assignment. Native release and retention remain usable during commerce cancellation or outage; unsafe Sync writeback stays held/local. No response creates a cancellation fee, invoice approval, journal, bank transfer, or EDI cancellation message.

## Investigate late carrier evidence

Correlation checks the exact attempt reference and its original partner/SCAC. A retired attempt's 990 is ignored for current ownership and retained in the audit. It cannot accept or decline a newer offer, including another offer to the same carrier. An ambiguous freight-reference fallback cannot identify a new attempt.

Historical 214 movement and 210 invoices create open carrier incidents. The original event remains intact; Freight does not move the replacement load or post the former carrier's invoice against its new buy agreement. Estimates alone do not create a physical-custody conflict. An incident pauses new tendering/dispatch and EDI handoffs, and prevents delivery evidence from qualifying finance approval/issuance.

In **Integrations → Inbound documents**, these signed documents show **Reconciliation required**, with a link to the load. Investigate with the carrier, then record the contact, external reference, and findings through **Resolve carrier conflict**. Resolution retains current ownership and all historical evidence. The inbox item becomes `reconciled`; its original processing result and attempt journal remain. It is not replayed as a new shipment event or invoice. If custody or liabilities need another action, record that verified action explicitly using the existing operational/finance workflows; this confirmation does not invent it.

## Legacy records

When an older assigned load first needs tender correlation or an operation, Freight snapshots its existing carrier and retains its original load-reference shipment identity. This is marked `legacy`, with creator `legacy_snapshot` and the time of adoption; it does not invent the original tender time. Missing transmission history remains uncertain. A confirmed release followed by a new tender establishes the new independent identity without rewriting old payloads.

## Gateway and commissioning boundary

The inspected `stateset-edi` `Tender204` builder emits `B2A*00` originals and exposes no cancellation purpose in that request model. Freight uses the gateway's supported original-offer endpoint and records external release evidence. Electronic cancellation/change messages, carrier-specific acknowledgment rules, transport certification, and production carrier acceptance remain commissioning work. A successful gateway response confirms generation/queuing, not delivery or carrier agreement.
